### 2c. FOLDERS ARE treated as games — `isPs3GameFolder`

`GameLibraryRepository.kt:422–444` (full body):
```kotlin
private fun isPs3GameFolder(directory: File): Boolean {
    fun child(vararg path: String): File? {
        var current: File = directory
        for (segment in path) {
            current = current.listFiles()
                ?.firstOrNull { it.name.equals(segment, ignoreCase = true) }
                ?: return null
        }
        return current
    }
    if (child("PS3_GAME", "PARAM.SFO")?.isFile == true) return true
    if (child("PS3_DISC.SFB")?.isFile == true) return true
    val sfo = child("PARAM.SFO")?.takeIf { it.isFile } ?: return false
    if (child("USRDIR")?.isDirectory != true) return false
    // ... data-install rejection ...
    return sfoCategory(sfo) != "GD"
}
```

**Exact constants recognised as "this folder IS a game":**

| Pattern | Meaning | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO` | JB folder dump (case-insensitive) | 432 |
| `PS3_DISC.SFB` | real disc rip (case-insensitive), alone is enough | 433 |
| `PARAM.SFO` + `USRDIR/` (dir) | installed/HDD game folder | 434–435 |
| `PARAM.SFO` CATEGORY `!= "GD"` | excludes game-data installs | 443 |

Notably **`game.iso` inside a folder is NOT how folders are recognised** — there is no such check. A folder containing only `game.iso` is *not* a game folder; the `.iso` is found by the normal file branch and listed individually.

Case-insensitivity is explicit (comment 418–420: FAT/exFAT → `PS3_GAME` as likely to be `ps3_game`).

**A game folder is a LEAF** — `scanRawDirectory:505–519`:
```kotlin
if (file.isDirectory) {
    // A game folder is a leaf: emit it and do NOT descend. ...
    if (runCatching { isPs3GameFolder(file) }.getOrDefault(false)) {
        val folderUri = Uri.fromFile(file)
        output.putIfAbsent(folderUri.toString(),
            createGame(folderUri, file.name, "folder", null, probeDisc(file)))
        return@forEach
    }
    scanRawDirectory(file, output, depth + 1)
    return@forEach
}
```
The pseudo-extension used for folders is the **literal string `"folder"`** (uppercased to `"FOLDER"` in `GameInfo.extension` by `createGame` line 640). Read back at line 220: `game.extension.equals("folder", ignoreCase = true)`.

231:             val uri = runCatching { rawUri.toUri() }.getOrNull() ?: return@forEach
232:             val posix = MainActivityRuntime.resolveTreeUriToPosix(rawUri)
233:             val rawRoot = if (canUseRawStorage()) posix?.let(::File) else null
234:             android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "dir=$rawUri -> posix=$posix isDir=${rawRoot?.isDirectory}")
235:             if (rawRoot?.isDirectory == true) {
236:                 shieldFromMediaScanner(rawRoot)
237:                 scanRawDirectory(rawRoot, collected, 0)
238:             } else {
239:                 // SAF fallback. Games found this way are LISTED but the core cannot boot them:
240:                 // it opens games with ordinary file IO and a document tree has no path to open.
241:                 // Without All files access every folder outside the emulator's own directory
242:                 // lands here, which reads as "the game is there but hangs on its loading
243:                 // screen" rather than as a permissions problem. Say which it is.
244:                 val tree = DocumentFile.fromTreeUri(context, uri)
245:                 if (!canUseRawStorage()) {
246:                     android.util.Log.w(
247:                         ScanTag,
248:                         "  $rawUri is being scanned over SAF because All files access is not " +
249:                             "granted. Games found here will appear in the library but cannot be " +
250:                             "read by the emulator -- grant the permission, or move them into " +
251:                             "the games directory inside the emulator folder."
252:                     )
253:                 } else {
254:                     android.util.Log.w(
255:                         ScanTag,
256:                         "  $rawUri has no filesystem path (posix=$posix); falling back to SAF. " +
257:                             "Games found here cannot be read by the emulator."
258:                     )
259:                 }
260:                 android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  SAF fallback: tree=${tree?.uri} canRead=${tree?.canRead()} children=${runCatching { tree?.listFiles()?.size }.getOrNull()}")
261:                 tree?.let { scanDocumentTree(it, collected, 0) }
262:             }
263:         }
264:         internalGameDirectories().forEach { dir ->
265:             android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "internal dir=${dir.absolutePath}")
266:             // dev_hdd0/game is the emulator's own install root and its shape is known: one
267:             // directory per title, nothing else. It gets the strict scan. Everything else is
268:             // a folder a user pointed us at, where games legitimately sit at any depth.
269:             if (dir.name == "game") scanInstalledTitles(dir, collected)
270:             else scanRawDirectory(dir, collected, 0)
271:         }
272:         val locked = lockedGamePaths()
273:         android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "scan done: ${collected.size} game(s), ${locked.size} locked")
274:         collected.values
275:             .map { game ->
276:                 val path = runCatching { game.uri.path?.let { File(it).canonicalPath } }.getOrNull()
277:                 if (path != null && path in locked) game.copy(locked = true) else game
278:             }
279:             .sortedBy { it.title.lowercase() }
280:             .also { saveCache(directories, it) }
281:     }

379:     private fun scanDocumentTree(
380:         directory: DocumentFile,
381:         output: MutableMap<String, GameInfo>,
382:         depth: Int,
383:     ) {
384:         if (depth > MaxScanDepth) return
385:         val children = runCatching { directory.listFiles() }.getOrNull() ?: return
386:         children.forEach { file ->
387:             if (file.isDirectory) {
388:                 // Same leaf rule as the raw scan. No SFO probe here: the core opens
389:                 // by path and a content:// tree has none to give, so the title comes
390:                 // from the folder name -- as it already does for a SAF-listed .iso.
391:                 if (runCatching { isPs3GameDocument(file) }.getOrDefault(false)) {
392:                     output.putIfAbsent(
393:                         file.uri.toString(),
394:                         createGame(file.uri, file.name ?: "", "folder", null),
395:                     )
396:                     return@forEach
397:                 }
398:                 scanDocumentTree(file, output, depth + 1)
399:                 return@forEach
400:             }
401:             val name = file.name ?: return@forEach
402:             val extension = name.substringAfterLast('.', "").lowercase()
403:             if (extension !in gameExtensions) return@forEach
404:             val probe = if (extension in probeExtensions) probeDocument(file.uri) else null
405:             output.putIfAbsent(file.uri.toString(), createGame(file.uri, name, extension, probe))
406:         }
407:     }

409:     /**
410:      * True when this directory IS a game rather than a folder containing games.
411:      *
412:      * Two shapes, both common and neither an .iso:
413:      *   - a JB folder dump, which keeps the disc layout: <dir>/PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO
414:      *     (PS3_DISC.SFB alongside it on a real disc rip)
415:      *   - an installed/HDD game folder -- PARAM.SFO next to USRDIR. This is what
416:      *     RPCS3's own games directory holds, and the shape prototypes that never
417:      *     got a retail master ship in.
418:      *
419:      * Case-insensitive: these come off FAT/exFAT cards and out of archives, so
420:      * "PS3_GAME" is as likely to be "ps3_game".
421:      */
422:     private fun isPs3GameFolder(directory: File): Boolean {
423:         fun child(vararg path: String): File? {
424:             var current: File = directory
425:             for (segment in path) {
426:                 current = current.listFiles()
427:                     ?.firstOrNull { it.name.equals(segment, ignoreCase = true) }
428:                     ?: return null
429:             }
430:             return current
431:         }
432:         if (child("PS3_GAME", "PARAM.SFO")?.isFile == true) return true
433:         if (child("PS3_DISC.SFB")?.isFile == true) return true
434:         val sfo = child("PARAM.SFO")?.takeIf { it.isFile } ?: return false
435:         if (child("USRDIR")?.isDirectory != true) return false
436:         // A game data install has this exact shape too, a PARAM.SFO next to USRDIR, so the
437:         // layout alone cannot tell it apart from an HDD game. It holds no EBOOT, so listing it
438:         // gave every title that installs data a second tile that cannot boot (Skate 3's 1.1 GB
439:         // BLUS30464_INSTALL, sitting next to the disc it belongs to). CATEGORY is what
440:         // separates them: GD is data, HG and DG are games. The native scanner already rejects
441:         // these because fetchGameInfo requires BOOTABLE and game data does not set it. This
442:         // applies the same rule to the folder path, which never opens the SFO at all.
443:         return sfoCategory(sfo) != "GD"
444:     }
445: 
446:     /**
447:      * CATEGORY out of a PARAM.SFO, or null when it cannot be read.
448:      *
449:      * A malformed or truncated file has to degrade to "list it" rather than hide a real game,
450:      * which is what [ParamSfo] answering null for every failure buys here.
451:      */
452:     private fun sfoCategory(sfo: File): String? = ParamSfo.string(sfo, "CATEGORY")
453: 
454:     /** [isPs3GameFolder] over a SAF tree. */
455:     private fun isPs3GameDocument(directory: DocumentFile): Boolean {
456:         val children = runCatching { directory.listFiles() }.getOrNull() ?: return false
457:         fun find(name: String) = children.firstOrNull { it.name.equals(name, ignoreCase = true) }
458:         if (find("PS3_DISC.SFB")?.isFile == true) return true
459:         find("PS3_GAME")?.takeIf { it.isDirectory }?.let { gameDir ->
460:             val inner = runCatching { gameDir.listFiles() }.getOrNull().orEmpty()
461:             if (inner.any { it.isFile && it.name.equals("PARAM.SFO", ignoreCase = true) }) return true
462:         }
463:         return find("PARAM.SFO")?.isFile == true && find("USRDIR")?.isDirectory == true
464:     }

466:     /**
467:      * dev_hdd0/game, scanned as what it is: one directory per installed title.
468:      *
469:      * The recursive scan cannot be used here. It descends into anything that is not itself a
470:      * game folder and then accepts any file whose extension is in [gameExtensions], and "img"
471:      * is one of those. A title's own data is full of them, so once a package unpacked its
472:      * contents over this directory rather than into a title folder of its own, GTA IV's
473:      * archives arrived in the library as games: manhat01, props_ab, vehicles, script,
474:      * weapons. Every one of them a .img sitting where the scanner was willing to look.
475:      *
476:      * The extractor no longer unpacks into this directory (see unpkg.cpp set_install_path),
477:      * but nothing should be relying on that to keep the library clean, and existing installs
478:      * still have the debris. A direct child here is a title or it is not listed.
479:      */
480:     private fun scanInstalledTitles(directory: File, output: MutableMap<String, GameInfo>) {
481:         val children = runCatching { directory.listFiles() }.getOrNull() ?: return
482:         children.forEach { file ->
483:             if (!file.isDirectory) return@forEach
484:             if (!runCatching { isPs3GameFolder(file) }.getOrDefault(false)) {
485:                 android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  skipping non-title '${file.name}' in dev_hdd0/game")
486:                 return@forEach
487:             }
488:             val uri = Uri.fromFile(file)
489:             android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  installed title '${file.name}'")
490:             output.putIfAbsent(
491:                 uri.toString(),
492:                 createGame(uri, file.name, "folder", null, probeDisc(file)),
493:             )
494:         }
495:     }

497:     private fun scanRawDirectory(
498:         directory: File,
499:         output: MutableMap<String, GameInfo>,
500:         depth: Int,
501:     ) {
502:         if (depth > MaxScanDepth) return
503:         val children = runCatching { directory.listFiles() }.getOrNull() ?: return
504:         children.forEach { file ->
505:             if (file.isDirectory) {
506:                 // A game folder is a leaf: emit it and do NOT descend. Descending
507:                 // also used to add USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN as its own bogus entry, since
508:                 // "bin" is in gameExtensions.
509:                 if (runCatching { isPs3GameFolder(file) }.getOrDefault(false)) {
510:                     val folderUri = Uri.fromFile(file)
511:                     android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  game folder '${file.name}'")
512:                     output.putIfAbsent(
513:                         folderUri.toString(),
514:                         createGame(folderUri, file.name, "folder", null, probeDisc(file)),
515:                     )
516:                     return@forEach
517:                 }
518:                 scanRawDirectory(file, output, depth + 1)
519:                 return@forEach
520:             }
521:             val extension = file.extension.lowercase()
522:             android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  raw file '${file.name}' ext=$extension accepted=${extension in gameExtensions}")
523:             if (extension !in gameExtensions) return@forEach
524:             val uri = Uri.fromFile(file)
525:             val disc = if (extension in probeExtensions) probeDisc(file) else null
526:             val probe = if (disc == null && extension in probeExtensions) probeRaw(file) else null
527:             output.putIfAbsent(uri.toString(), createGame(uri, file.name, extension, probe, disc))
528:         }
529:     }

531:     /**
532:      * Drop the separator, but only from something that actually looks like a title ID.
533:      *
534:      * The check is not about which console the game is for -- this emulator runs PS3 titles
535:      * and nothing else. It is about not manufacturing an identity out of a guess.
536:      * FilenameParser takes the first four-letters + five-digits token it finds ANYWHERE in
537:      * the name and reconstructs it in the PS2 dump shape it was written for, so what arrives
538:      * here may be a real id (BLUS-30917), a token out of a release tag, or an id belonging to
539:      * a different game entirely.
540:      *
541:      * Left hyphenated, a bad guess matches nothing: no cover, no disc icon, no config, and
542:      * the card shows a placeholder. That is a visible failure and it is the safe one.
543:      * Stripped, the same guess becomes a WELL-FORMED title id and quietly resolves whatever
544:      * is filed under it -- another game's cover and curated name, and its config_db entry,
545:      * which the core applies at boot. So normalise only what carries a real PS3 prefix:
546:      * B for disc releases (BLUS/BLES/BCUS...), N for PSN (NPUB/NPEB...).
547:      *
548:      * Deliberately NOT gated on [GamePlatform]: that enum comes from the same probe that
549:      * produced the serial, so in the one case this function exists for -- the probe failed
550:      * and the name came off the filename -- it carries no information at all.
551:      */
552:     private fun normalizeSerial(raw: String): String {
553:         val stripped = raw.replace("-", "")
554:         return if (ps3SerialRegex.matches(stripped)) stripped else raw
555:     }
556: 
557:     /**
558:      * Carry a game's per-serial data across an identity correction.
559:      *
560:      * The serial is not just the cover key: it keys config.game.<serial>, per-game core
561:      * overrides, touch layouts and profiles, pad bindings, play time, the pinned name and
562:      * the custom cover file. Renaming the game without moving those silently resets every
563:      * one of them, and nothing prunes the old keys afterwards, so they become unreachable
564:      * rather than merely unused.
565:      *
566:      * A same-named key already under the new id is overwritten. It can only have come from
567:      * an earlier scan that probed the disc successfully, before this entry regressed to a
568:      * filename-derived id; the hyphenated one is what the game has actually been running
569:      * with since, so it is the live value and the older one is stale.
570:      */
571:     private fun migrateSerialKeys(old: String, new: String) {
572:         runCatching {
573:             val prefs = MainActivityRuntime.prefs
574:             val snapshot = prefs.all
575:             val moved = snapshot.keys.filter { it.contains(old) }
576:             if (moved.isNotEmpty()) {
577:                 prefs.edit().apply {
578:                     moved.forEach { key ->
579:                         when (val value = snapshot[key]) {
580:                             is String -> putString(key.replace(old, new), value)
581:                             is Int -> putInt(key.replace(old, new), value)
582:                             is Long -> putLong(key.replace(old, new), value)
583:                             is Boolean -> putBoolean(key.replace(old, new), value)
584:                             is Float -> putFloat(key.replace(old, new), value)
585:                             is Set<*> -> @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
586:                                 putStringSet(key.replace(old, new), value as Set<String>)
587:                             else -> return@forEach
588:                         }
589:                         remove(key)
590:                     }
591:                 }.apply()
592:             }
593:             CustomCovers.renameSerial(context, old, new)
594:             android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "serial '$old' -> '$new' (${moved.size} pref key(s) moved)")
595:         }
596:     }

598:     private fun createGame(
599:         uri: Uri,
600:         name: String,
601:         extension: String,
602:         rawProbe: String?,
603:         disc: DiscInfo? = null,
604:     ): GameInfo {
605:         val (probeSerial, probePlatform) = parseProbe(rawProbe)
606:         val (fileTitle, fileSerial) = FilenameParser.parse(name)
607:         val platform = if (disc != null) GamePlatform.PS3 else probePlatform ?: GamePlatform.PS3
608:         // The disc's own PARAM.SFO wins: it is the authoritative title ID, where
609:         // a filename-derived one is a guess off a dump's naming convention.
610:         //
611:         // Normalise the result: FilenameParser reconstructs every serial in the PS2 dump
612:         // shape (SLUS-20312) because that is the convention its regex was written for, so a
613:         // PS3 game whose serial came off the filename is recorded as BLUS-30917 and matches
614:         // nothing -- not the cover repo (keyed by the exact PARAM.SFO id), not disc-icons,
615:         // not config.game.<serial>. Doing it here rather than in FilenameParser is what
616:         // repairs the entries already cached: they are re-seeded into discInfoCache on every
617:         // scan and arrive back here as disc.titleId, which has top priority.
618:         val rawSerial = disc?.titleId ?: probeSerial ?: fileSerial
619:         val serial = rawSerial?.let(::normalizeSerial)
620:         if (rawSerial != null && serial != null && rawSerial != serial) {
621:             migrateSerialKeys(rawSerial, serial)
622:         }
623:         val compatibility = serial
624:             ?.let { runCatching { NativeApp.getCompatibilityForSerial(it) }.getOrDefault(0) }
625:             ?.minus(1)
626:             ?.coerceIn(0, 5)
627:             ?: 0
628:         // GameDB title first, filename only as the fallback — the same order GameList.cpp
629:         // uses. The database is the curated name: it drops dump cruft ("(USA) [!] v1.1"),
630:         // and for a Japanese game it is the ACTUAL Japanese title, which no filename-derived
631:         // guess can produce. Issue #338.
632:         val db = serial?.let { dbTitles(it) }
633:         return GameInfo(
634:             uri = uri,
635:             title = disc?.title?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
636:                 ?: db?.name?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
637:                 ?: fileTitle,
638:             serial = serial,
639:             compatibility = compatibility,
640:             extension = extension.uppercase(),
641:             platform = platform,
642:             // Only meaningful alongside a DB title; a filename-derived one has no sort key
643:             // and is not a translation of anything.
644:             titleSort = db?.sort.orEmpty(),
645:             titleEn = db?.en.orEmpty(),
646:         )
647:     }

649:     private data class DbTitles(val name: String, val sort: String, val en: String)
650: 
651:     /** GameDB's three titles for [serial], or null when it isn't in the database. */
652:     private fun dbTitles(serial: String): DbTitles? {
653:         val raw = runCatching { NativeApp.getTitlesForSerial(serial) }.getOrNull()
654:         if (raw.isNullOrEmpty()) return null
655:         // "<name>\n<name-sort>\n<name-en>" — split with a limit so a title can't lose a
656:         // trailing field, and tolerate a short string from an older core.
657:         val parts = raw.split('\n')
658:         val name = parts.getOrNull(0).orEmpty()
659:         if (name.isEmpty()) return null
660:         return DbTitles(name, parts.getOrNull(1).orEmpty(), parts.getOrNull(2).orEmpty())
661:     }

663:     private fun parseProbe(value: String?): Pair<String?, GamePlatform?> {
664:         if (value.isNullOrBlank()) return null to null
665:         val separator = value.indexOf(':')
666:         if (separator <= 0) return value to null
667:         return value.substring(separator + 1) to GamePlatform.fromKey(value.substring(0, separator))
668:     }

671:         val descriptor = context.contentResolver.openFileDescriptor(uri, "r") ?: return null
672:         NativeApp.getGameSerialFromFd(descriptor.detachFd())
673:     }.getOrNull()

675:     private fun probeRaw(file: File): String? = runCatching {
676:         val descriptor = ParcelFileDescriptor.open(file, ParcelFileDescriptor.MODE_READ_ONLY)
677:         NativeApp.getGameSerialFromFd(descriptor.detachFd())
678:     }.getOrNull()

680:     /**
681:      * Read a PS3 disc's title ID, title and cover from the image itself.
682:      *
683:      * The inherited probe looks for a PS2 SYSTEM.CNF, so every PS3 ISO came back
684:      * with no serial -- and no serial meant no title, no compatibility entry and
685:      * no cover. This asks the core to mount the ISO and read PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO,
686:      * extracting PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG alongside it.
687:      *
688:      * Only for POSIX paths: the core opens the image by path, so a content:// URI
689:      * has nothing to hand it. That is not a real gap here -- the raw scan path is
690:      * the one that runs whenever all-files access is granted, which is required
691:      * for the emulator to read the disc at boot anyway.
692:      */
693:     private fun probeDisc(file: File): DiscInfo? {
694:         // One extraction per game: re-reading a 7 GB image on every rescan to
695:         // recover a PNG we already have would make each scan take minutes.
696:         val existing = discInfoCache[file.absolutePath]
697:         if (existing != null) return existing
698: 
699:         val raw = runCatching {
700:             RPCSX.instance.probeDiscInfo(file.absolutePath, DiscIcons.fileFor(PendingIcon).absolutePath)
701:         }.getOrNull()
702:         android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  probeDiscInfo('${file.name}') -> $raw")
703:         if (raw == null) return null
704: 
705:         val info = runCatching {
706:             val o = JSONObject(raw)
707:             val id = o.optString("titleId")
708:             if (id.isBlank()) return@runCatching null
709:             // The probe writes to a fixed staging name because it cannot know the
710:             // title ID until it has already parsed the SFO.
711:             if (o.optBoolean("icon")) {
712:                 val staged = DiscIcons.fileFor(PendingIcon)
713:                 val target = DiscIcons.fileFor(id)
714:                 // renameTo answers false instead of throwing when the target already exists,
715:                 // and the answer was discarded: a re-extraction for a title that already had

package com.xeno

import java.io.File

/**
 * Cover art extracted from PS3 discs.
 *
 * XENO fetched covers from a GitHub repo keyed by serial. There is no
 * equivalent repo for the PS3, but there is something better: every disc
 * carries its own artwork at PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG -- the image the console shows
 * on the XMB, and the one desktop RPCS3 shows in its game grid.
 *
 * The scanner extracts it once, on the pass that reads PARAM.SFO for the title
 * ID, so a cover costs nothing after the first scan: no network, no 404s, and
 * it always matches the disc it came from.
 *
 * Keyed by title ID (BLUS30464, BCES01234, ...), which is what PARAM.SFO gives
 * us and what everything else in the app already uses as the serial.
 */
object DiscIcons {

    private fun dir(): File =
        File(XenoApplication.appContext.filesDir, "disc-icons").apply { mkdirs() }

    fun fileFor(titleId: String): File = File(dir(), "$titleId.png")

    /**
     * True when this game's icon has already been extracted.
     *
     * Length, not isFile: an empty file is indistinguishable from a real one to isFile, and
     * it is a shape this can actually end up in -- the extraction writes to a staging name
     * and renames, and neither the write nor the rename is checked. An empty icon then reads
     * as "already extracted" forever, and the card falls through to the text placeholder
     * because there is nothing for Coil to decode. Requiring bytes makes that self-repairing:
     * the next scan re-probes and overwrites it.
     */
    fun has(titleId: String): Boolean = fileFor(titleId).length() > 0L

    fun clear() {
        runCatching { dir().listFiles()?.forEach { it.delete() } }
    }
}

<content>
1: # Docker ARM64 APK build for XENO / ARMS3.
2: #
3: # The whole Android build (LLVM in-tree + RPCS3 core + Gradle UI) runs inside
4: # `xeno-android-ci`, the toolchain image staged in .ci/Dockerfile.android, so a
5: # job only needs a stock ubuntu-24.04 runner + Docker. No Windows, no manual SDK
6: # setup on the runner.
7: #
8: # Robustness contract:
9: #   * the toolchain image is cached with docker layer cache (type=gha), so the
10: #     SDK/NDK never need re-downloading between runs;
11: #   * the warm build-a13 dir and the Gradle dependency cache are restored/saved
12: #     with actions/cache, keyed exactly like the Windows release workflow;
13: #   * an interrupted build STILL saves its caches (ninja is incremental), and the
14: #     build step retries up to 3 times to ride out flaky pulls;
15: #   * cache saves are best-effort (continue-on-error) - a cache problem must
16: #     never fail an otherwise green build.
17: 
18: name: Docker ARM64 APK
19: 
20: on:
21:   push:
22:     branches:
23:       - master
24:     tags:
25:       - "0.*"
26:   workflow_dispatch:
27:     inputs:
28:       variant:
29:         description: APK ISA/API variant (legacy, a11, a13, a15)
30:         default: "a13"
31: 
32: concurrency:
33:   group: docker-arm64-apk-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name }}
34:   cancel-in-progress: true
35: 
36: jobs:
37:   build:
38:     name: Build ARM64 APK in Docker
39:     runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
40:     timeout-minutes: 360
41:     permissions:
42:       contents: write
43: 
44:     steps:
45:       - name: Checkout with submodules
46:         uses: actions/checkout@v5
47:         with:
48:           fetch-depth: 0
49:           submodules: recursive
50: 
51:       # Cache keys are cheap O(1) git hash-objects. The warm build dir is keyed
52:       # on the LLVM submodule PIN (not hashFiles over the LLVM tree, which is
53:       # cancelled by GitHub after 120 s) plus a recipe fingerprint of the few
54:       # scripts that actually change cmake arguments.
55:       - name: Compute cache keys
56:         id: cache-keys
57:         shell: bash
58:         run: |
59:           # shellcheck disable=SC2086
60:           LLVM_PIN="$(git -C 3rdparty/llvm/llvm rev-parse --short=12 HEAD)"
61:           echo "llvm=${LLVM_PIN}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
62: 
63:           RECIPE="$(git hash-object \
64:               android/configure.sh \
65:               android/build-variants.sh \
66:               android/stamp-git-version.sh | sha1sum | cut -c1-12)"
67:           echo "a13-bin-key=xeno-docker-build-a13-${{ github.ref_name }}-llvm-${LLVM_PIN}-cfg-${RECIPE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
68: 
69:           GRADLE_FILES="android/armsx3-ui/settings.gradle.kts
70:                         android/armsx3-ui/gradle.properties
71:                         android/armsx3-ui/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties
72:                         android/armsx3-ui/app/build.gradle.kts"
73:           [ -f android/armsx3-ui/gradle/libs.versions.toml ] && \
74:             GRADLE_FILES="$GRADLE_FILES android/armsx3-ui/gradle/libs.versions.toml"
75:           # Word-splitting GRADLE_FILES is the point; it is a newline-separated file list.
76:           # shellcheck disable=SC2086
77:           GRADLE_CFG="$(git hash-object $GRADLE_FILES | sha1sum | cut -c1-12)"
78:           echo "gradle-key=gradle-Linux-${GRADLE_CFG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
79: 
80:           # Park everything Gradle needs inside the workspace so the whole cache
81:           # is one self-contained directory (same trick as the Windows flow).
82:           echo "GRADLE_USER_HOME=${{ github.workspace }}/.gradle" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
83: 
84:       - name: Restore a13 build dir
85:         uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
86:         id: build-cache
87:         with:
88:           path: ${{ github.workspace }}/build-a13
89:           key: ${{ steps.cache-keys.outputs.a13-bin-key }}
90:           restore-keys: |
91:             xeno-docker-build-a13-
92: 
93:       - name: Restore Gradle cache
94:         uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
95:         id: gradle-cache
96:         with:
97:           path: ${{ github.workspace }}/.gradle
98:           key: ${{ steps.cache-keys.outputs.gradle-key }}
99:           restore-keys: |
100:             gradle-Linux-
101: 
102:       # Fast-forward the restored LLVM build tree.
103:       #
104:       # A restored cache hands the objects back with their ORIGINAL mtimes, and
105:       # the fresh git checkout re-stamps every source with a NEWER mtime, so
106:       # ninja considers all ~3000 LLVM objects stale and rebuilds them (a ~50
107:       # minute nop). Bumping only the LLVM subtree's mtimes up to "now" makes
108:       # ninja see it as up to date; RPCS3/3rdparty objects are left alone so a
109:       # real core change still recompiles. This is safe ONLY when the cache that
110:       # was restored was built from the current LLVM pin -- check that the
111:       # matched key carries the exact llvm-<sha> we are about to build, and skip
112:       # the fast-forward otherwise so a toolchain bump rebuilds from scratch.
113:       - name: Fast-forward restored LLVM build tree
114:         if: steps.build-cache.outputs.cache-matched-key != ''
115:         shell: bash
116:         run: |
117:           CURRENT_LLVM="llvm-$(git -C 3rdparty/llvm/llvm rev-parse --short=12 HEAD)"
118:           if [[ "${{ steps.build-cache.outputs.cache-matched-key }}" == *"$CURRENT_LLVM"* ]]; then
119:             find "${{ github.workspace }}/build-a13/3rdparty/llvm/llvm_build" -exec touch {} + 2>/dev/null || true
120:             echo "fast-forwarded restored LLVM tree for ${CURRENT_LLVM}"
121:           else
122:             echo "restored cache is from a different LLVM pin, leaving mtimes untouched"
123:           fi
124: 
125:       # The image rarely changes; type=gha layer cache restores the SDK/NDK
126:       # layers in seconds on every run instead of re-staging ~4 GB up front.
127:       - name: Set up Docker Buildx
128:         uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
129:         with:
130:           driver: docker-container
131:           driver-opts: |
132:             image=moby/buildkit:latest
133:             network=host
134: 
135:       - name: Build toolchain image (cached)
136:         uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
137:         with:
138:           context: .ci
139:           file: .ci/Dockerfile.android
140:           push: false
141:           load: true
142:           tags: xeno-android-ci:latest
143:           cache-from: type=gha,scope=xeno-android-ci
144:           cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=xeno-android-ci
145: 
146:       # librashader and libadrenotools are not submodules upstream; fetched by
147:       # hand per the repository README.
148:       - name: Fetch librashader
149:         run: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/SnowflakePowered/librashader 3rdparty/librashader
150: 
151:       - name: Fetch libadrenotools
152:         run: git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/bylaws/libadrenotools android/armsx3-ui/app/src/main/cpp/libadrenotools
153: 
154:       # The actual build, fully inside the container. The workspace is mounted
155:       # read-write at /src so build-a13 and the gradle cache live under the
156:       # workspace and are saved by the cache steps below. OUT_DIR is /src/out
157:       # so the APK lands on the mounted volume for artifacts.
158:       - name: Build ARM64 APK in Docker container
159:         shell: bash
160:         env:
161:           VARIANTS: "${{ github.event.inputs.variant || 'a13' }}"
162:         run: |
163:           # OUT_DIR is /src/out; build-variants.sh does not mkdir it, and the
164:           # bind mount only creates /src, so the final APK copy would fail
165:           # "No such file or directory" without this.
166:           mkdir -p "${{ github.workspace }}/out"
167: 
168:           # Retry the whole build (ninja is incremental, so re-entry is cheap;
169:           # the exposure is Gradle pulling resolve-time deps on a cold cache).

#
# The whole Android build (LLVM in-tree + RPCS3 core + Gradle UI) runs inside
# `xeno-android-ci`, the toolchain image staged in .ci/Dockerfile.android, so a
# job only needs a stock ubuntu-24.04 runner + Docker. No Windows, no manual SDK
# setup on the runner.
#
# Robustness contract:
#   * the toolchain image is cached with docker layer cache (type=gha), so the
#     SDK/NDK never need re-downloading between runs;
#   * the warm build-a13 dir and the Gradle dependency cache are restored/saved
#     with actions/cache, keyed exactly like the Windows release workflow;
#   * an interrupted build STILL saves its caches (ninja is incremental), and the
#     build step retries up to 3 times to ride out flaky pulls;
#   * cache saves are best-effort (continue-on-error) - a cache problem must
#     never fail an otherwise green build.

display.text:
# Docker ARM64 APK build for XENO / ARMS3.
#
# The whole Android build (LLVM in-tree + RPCS3 core + Gradle UI) runs inside
# `xeno-android-ci`, the toolchain image staged in .ci/Dockerfile.android, so a
# job only needs a stock ubuntu-24.04 runner + Docker. No Windows, no manual SDK
# setup on the runner.
#
# Robustness contract:
#   * the toolchain image is cached with docker layer cache (type=gha), so the
#     SDK/NDK never need re-downloading between runs;
#   * the warm build-a13 dir and the Gradle dependency cache are restored/saved
#     with actions/cache, keyed exactly like the Windows release workflow;
#   * an interrupted build STILL saves its caches (ninja is incremental), and the
#     build step retries up to 3 times to ride out flaky pulls;
#   * cache saves are best-effort (continue-on-error) - a cache problem must
#     never fail an otherwise green build.

name: Docker ARM64 APK

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
    tags:
      - "0.*"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      variant:
        description: APK ISA/API variant (legacy, a11, a13, a15)
        default: "a13"

concurrency:
  group: docker-arm64-apk-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build ARM64 APK in Docker
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout with submodules
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          submodules: recursive

      # Cache keys are cheap O(1) git hash-objects. The warm build dir is keyed
      # on the LLVM submodule PIN (not hashFiles over the LLVM tree, which is
      # cancelled by GitHub after 120 s) plus a recipe fingerprint of the few
      # scripts that actually change cmake arguments.
      - name: Compute cache keys
        id: cache-keys
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          LLVM_PIN="$(git -C 3rdparty/llvm/llvm rev-parse --short=12 HEAD)"
          echo "llvm=${LLVM_PIN}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          RECIPE="$(git hash-object \
              android/configure.sh \
              android/build-variants.sh \
              android/stamp-git-version.sh | sha1sum | cut -c1-12)"
          echo "a13-bin-key=xeno-docker-build-a13-${{ github.ref_name }}-llvm-${LLVM_PIN}-cfg-${RECIPE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          GRADLE_FILES="android/armsx3-ui/settings.gradle.kts
                        android/armsx3-ui/gradle.properties
                        android/armsx3-ui/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties
                        android/armsx3-ui/app/build.gradle.kts"
          [ -f android/armsx3-ui/gradle/libs.versions.toml ] && \
            GRADLE_FILES="$GRADLE_FILES android/armsx3-ui/gradle/libs.versions.toml"
          # Word-splitting GRADLE_FILES is the point; it is a newline-separated file list.
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          GRADLE_CFG="$(git hash-object $GRADLE_FILES | sha1sum | cut -c1-12)"
          echo "gradle-key=gradle-Linux-${GRADLE_CFG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # Park everything Gradle needs inside the workspace so the whole cache
          # is one self-contained directory (same trick as the Windows flow).
          echo "GRADLE_USER_HOME=${{ github.workspace }}/.gradle" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Restore a13 build dir
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        id: build-cache
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/build-a13
          key: ${{ steps.cache-keys.outputs.a13-bin-key }}
          restore-keys: |
            xeno-docker-build-a13-

      - name: Restore Gradle cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        id: gradle-cache
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/.gradle
          key: ${{ steps.cache-keys.outputs.gradle-key }}
          restore-keys: |
            gradle-Linux-

      # Fast-forward the restored LLVM build tree.
      #
      # A restored cache hands the objects back with their ORIGINAL mtimes, and
      # the fresh git checkout re-stamps every source with a NEWER mtime, so
      # ninja considers all ~3000 LLVM objects stale and rebuilds them (a ~50
      # minute nop). Bumping only the LLVM subtree's mtimes up to "now" makes
      # ninja see it as up to date; RPCS3/3rdparty objects are left alone so a
      # real core change still recompiles. This is safe ONLY when the cache that
      # was restored was built from the current LLVM pin -- check that the
      # matched key carries the exact llvm-<sha> we are about to build, and skip
      # the fast-forward otherwise so a toolchain bump rebuilds from scratch.
      - name: Fast-forward restored LLVM build tree
        if: steps.build-cache.outputs.cache-matched-key != ''
        shell: bash
        run: |
          CURRENT_LLVM="llvm-$(git -C 3rdparty/llvm/llvm rev-parse --short=12 HEAD)"
          if [[ "${{ steps.build-cache.outputs.cache-matched-key }}" == *"$CURRENT_LLVM"* ]]; then
            find "${{ github.workspace }}/build-a13/3rdparty/llvm/llvm_build" -exec touch {} + 2>/dev/null || true
            echo "fast-forwarded restored LLVM tree for ${CURRENT_LLVM}"
          else
            echo "restored cache is from a different LLVM pin, leaving mtimes untouched"
          fi

      # The image rarely changes; type=gha layer cache restores the SDK/NDK
      # layers in seconds on every run instead of re-staging ~4 GB up front.
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
        with:
          driver: docker-container
          driver-opts: |
            image=moby/buildkit:latest
            network=host

      - name: Build toolchain image (cached)
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .ci
          file: .ci/Dockerfile.android
          push: false
          load: true
          tags: xeno-android-ci:latest
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=xeno-android-ci
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=xeno-android-ci

      # librashader and libadrenotools are not submodules upstream; fetched by
      # hand per the repository README.
      - name: Fetch librashader
        run: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/SnowflakePowered/librashader 3rdparty/librashader

      - name: Fetch libadrenotools
        run: git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/bylaws/libadrenotools android/armsx3-ui/app/src/main/cpp/libadrenotools

      # The actual build, fully inside the container. The workspace is mounted
      # read-write at /src so build-a13 and the gradle cache live under the
      # workspace and are saved by the cache steps below. OUT_DIR is /src/out
      # so the APK lands on the mounted volume for artifacts.
      - name: Build ARM64 APK in Docker container
        shell: bash
        env:
          VARIANTS: "${{ github.event.inputs.variant || 'a13' }}"
        run: |
          # OUT_DIR is /src/out; build-variants.sh does not mkdir it, and the
          # bind mount only creates /src, so the final APK copy would fail
          # "No such file or directory" without this.
          mkdir -p "${{ github.workspace }}/out"

          # Retry the whole build (ninja is incremental, so re-entry is cheap;
          # the exposure is Gradle pulling resolve-time deps on a cold cache).
          status=1
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            if docker run --rm \
                -v "${{ github.workspace }}:/src" \
                -w /src \
                -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
                -e ANDROID_HOME=/opt/android-sdk \
                -e JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64 \
                -e GRADLE_USER_HOME=/src/.gradle \
                -e OUT_DIR=/src/out \
                -e CMAKE_VERSION=3.30.5 \
                -e VARIANTS="$VARIANTS" \
                xeno-android-ci:latest \
                bash android/build-variants.sh; then
              status=0
              break
            fi
            echo "::warning::build attempt $i failed, retrying in 20s"
            sleep 20
          done
          if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::build failed after 3 attempts"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "APK_NAME=$(find "${{ github.workspace }}/out" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.apk' -printf '%f\n' | head -1)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Upload APK artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: xeno-arm64-apk-docker
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/out/*.apk
          if-no-files-found: error

      # Save under run-unique keys so a partially built (possibly failed) dir is
      # still cached - ninja resumes it next run. Runs even when build failed.
      - name: Save a13 build dir
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/build-a13
          key: ${{ steps.cache-keys.outputs.a13-bin-key }}-${{ github.run_id }}

      - name: Save Gradle cache
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/.gradle
          key: ${{ steps.cache-keys.outputs.gradle-key }}-${{ github.run_id }}

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        # Manual dispatches on master are for producing an artifact, not a
        # release; publication only makes sense for a tag. The `gh release view`
        # guard makes a duplicate (e.g. the Windows workflow already released
        # the same tag) harmless instead of a red run.
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')
        run: |
          if gh release view "${{ github.ref_name }}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "::warning::release ${{ github.ref_name }} already exists, skipping"
          else
            gh release create "${{ github.ref_name }}" \
              --title "XENO ${{ github.ref_name }}" \
              --notes "ARMS3 APK (arm64-v8a), Docker build - run ${{ github.run_id }}. The emulator core (libxeno-core.so) ships as a separate asset: the app downloads it into private storage on first setup (Winlator-style), which is how the APK stays ~60 MB smaller. Do not rename the asset." \
              ${{ github.workspace }}/out/*.apk \
              ${{ github.workspace }}/android/armsx3-ui/app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libxeno-core.so
          fi
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

parts.text:
Found the build bug: `:app:mergeGithubReleaseJavaResource` fails — duplicate `META-INF/INDEX.LIST` from two Google auth jars. This is a Gradle packaging issue that needs a `packaging { resources { pickFirst / excludes } }` block in `app/build.gradle.kts`.

Importantly: the C++ core BUILDS FINE ([3045/3045] Linking CXX shared library android/libxeno-core.so). The failure is purely in the Gradle packaging step. So it's a quick fix.

Now let me plan:

**Task list:**
1. Fix build: `META-INF/INDEX.LIST` duplicate → add packaging block in `app/build.gradle.kts`.
2. Fix library junk entries (non-games shown).
3. Fix game not launching (InvalidFileOrFolder).
4. Commit, push, watch CI, fix remaining build errors.

For 2 and 3 I need to determine the root causes. Let me look at build.gradle.kts first, and think about the scanner.

Now let me think REALLY carefully about the junk entries, because this is the crux.

The junk: `ARMSX3.log`, `CEFramework` ×2, `CEHtmlApi` ×2, `CEHtmlUI` ×2, `CEPhWeb` ×2, `ps1_rom`.

Recall: displayed title = `disc?.title ?: db?.name ?: fileTitle` where `fileTitle = FilenameParser.parse(name).first` = `name.substringBeforeLast('.')` cleaned.

So:
- `ARMSX3.log` displayed → could be file `ARMSX3.log.bin`? or `ARMSX3.log.iso`? Hmm, `ARMSX3.log` is a real log file the app writes. But wait — the *title* strips the LAST extension. So file `ARMSX3.log` → substringBeforeLast('.') = "ARMSX3" → title "ARMSX3". Not matching. So the file must be named something like `ARMSX3.log.something-in-gameExtensions`.

Hmm! OR the title came from `disc?.title` (PARAM.SFO TITLE) — and FilenameParser wasn't involved.

Hmm, hold on, let's reconsider: what if these are FOLDERS recognized by `isPs3GameFolder`, and their displayed title comes from `probeDisc(file)` → PARAM.SFO TITLE?

**AH. I think I've got it!**

The user's ROM directory is the **shared storage root** (`/storage/emulated/0`) — "одна общая папка" = "one common folder". And `scanRawDirectory` recurses up to depth 12 through EVERYTHING, including:
- `Android/data/com.xxx.../files/`
- `xeno/config/dev_hdd0/game/<TITLE_ID>/` ← PS3 homebrew installs!

And Cheat Engine for PS3 — there IS a PS3 Cheat Engine. If the user installed it (or it's a PS3 homebrew app), dev_hdd0/game would have folders for it. But each folder = one title with one PARAM.SFO → one title name. The names CEFramework/CEHtmlApi/CEHtmlUI/CEPhWeb would each need their own folder...

```kotlin
fun string(bytes: ByteArray, key: String): String? {
    val buffer = java.nio.ByteBuffer.wrap(bytes).order(java.nio.ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN)
    if (bytes.size < 20 || buffer.getInt(0) != 0x46535000) return null
    val keyTable = buffer.getInt(8)
    val dataTable = buffer.getInt(12)
    for (index in 0 until buffer.getInt(16)) {
        val entry = 20 + index * 16
        if (entry + 16 > bytes.size) break
        val keyStart = keyTable + (buffer.getShort(entry).toInt() and 0xFFFF)
        if (keyStart < 0 || keyStart >= bytes.size) break
        var keyEnd = keyStart
        while (keyEnd < bytes.size && bytes[keyEnd] != 0.toByte()) keyEnd++
        if (String(bytes, keyStart, keyEnd - keyStart) != key) continue
        val dataStart = dataTable + buffer.getInt(entry + 12)
        val dataLength = buffer.getInt(entry + 4)
        if (dataStart < 0 || dataLength < 0 || dataStart + dataLength > bytes.size) break
        return String(bytes, dataStart, dataLength, Charsets.UTF_8).trimEnd('\u0000', ' ')
    }
    return null
}
```

Note: `buffer.getInt(0) != 0x46535000` — magic is read little-endian; "\0PSF" bytes are 00 50 53 46; read as LE int = 0x46535000. Correct.

```kotlin
internal object ParamSfo {
    fun string(sfo: File, key: String): String? =
        runCatching { string(sfo.readBytes(), key) }.getOrNull()

    fun int(sfo: File, key: String): Int? =
        runCatching { int(sfo.readBytes(), key) }.getOrNull()

    fun string(bytes: ByteArray, key: String): String? {
        val entry = entry(bytes, key) ?: return null
        return String(bytes, entry.offset, entry.length, Charsets.UTF_8).trimEnd('\u0000', ' ')
    }

    fun int(bytes: ByteArray, key: String): Int? {
        val entry = entry(bytes, key) ?: return null
        if (entry.length < 4) return null
        return java.nio.ByteBuffer.wrap(bytes, entry.offset, 4)
            .order(java.nio.ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN).int
    }

    /**
     * Locate a key's data range...
     */
    private class Entry(val offset: Int, val length: Int)

    private fun entry(bytes: ByteArray, key: String): Entry? {
        val buffer = java.nio.ByteBuffer.wrap(bytes).order(java.nio.ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN)
        // "\0PSF", then key-table start, data-table start, entry count.
        if (bytes.size < 20 || buffer.getInt(0) != 0x46535000) return null
        val keyTable = buffer.getInt(8)
        val dataTable = buffer.getInt(12)
        for (index in 0 until buffer.getInt(16)) {
            val entry = 20 + index * 16
            if (entry + 16 > bytes.size) break
            val keyStart = keyTable + (buffer.getShort(entry).toInt() and 0xFFFF)
            if (keyStart < 0 || keyStart >= bytes.size) break
            var keyEnd = keyStart
            while (keyEnd < bytes.size && bytes[keyEnd] != 0.toByte()) keyEnd++
            if (String(bytes, keyStart, keyEnd - keyStart) != key) continue
            val dataStart = dataTable + buffer.getInt(entry + 12)
            val dataLength = buffer.getInt(entry + 4)
            if (dataStart < 0 || dataLength < 0 || dataStart + dataLength > bytes.size) break
            return Entry(dataStart, dataLength)
        }
        return null
    }
}
```

Was the OLD code accepting it? Old code: `if (child("USRDIR")?.isDirectory != true) return false` — also rejected! So the old code ALSO rejected root-EBOOT-without-USRDIR.

Hmm, so my test expectation was wrong relative to both old and new behaviour. But: is the new gate correct? The old code required USRDIR for the PARAM.SFO case. My new code preserves that. And `EBOOT.BIN` at root is in EBOOT_PATHS (mirroring the core) but is only reachable via `PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO`... no, `PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN` is reachable.

So: for `discSfo != null` (PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO), the USRDIR gate is skipped, and hasBootableEboot checks EBOOT.BIN at root, USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN, USRDIR/ISO.BIN.EDAT, PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN. Good.

#!/bin/bash
# Regenerate the standalone scanner harness from the real Android source, so the
# fixtures in ScannerTest.kt exercise the shipped logic instead of a retyped copy.
#
# Two edits are applied to the extracted text, both harness-only:
#   android.util.Log.i(  -> ScanLog.i(   (collect the decisions instead of logging)
#   "    private fun "   -> "    fun "    (so ScannerTest can call the entry point)
set -euo pipefail

SRC=/home/runner/hub-work/xeno/code/android/armsx3-ui/app/src/main/java/com/xeno/data/library/GameLibraryRepository.kt
OUT=/home/runner/hub-work/xeno/tmp/Scanner.kt

# Block 1: isPs3GameFolder .. sfoCategory, i.e. the folder-classification logic.
S1=$(grep -n '^     \* True when this directory IS a game' "$SRC" | cut -d: -f1)
S1=$((S1 - 1))                                    # the '/**' line above it
E1=$(grep -n '^    private fun sfoCategory' "$SRC" | cut -d: -f1)

# Block 2: the ParamSfo object, from 'internal object' to its closing brace at column 0.
S2=$(grep -n '^internal object ParamSfo' "$SRC" | cut -d: -f1)
E2=$(awk -v s="$S2" 'NR > s && $0 == "}" { print NR; exit }' "$SRC")

{
  echo "package com.xeno"
  echo ""
  echo "import java.io.File"
  echo ""
  echo "// GENERATED by gen-harness.sh -- do not edit. Source: GameLibraryRepository.kt"
  echo "// lines $S1-$E1 (folder classification) and $S2-$E2 (ParamSfo)."
  echo "object ScanLog {"
  echo "    val lines = mutableListOf<String>()"
  echo '    fun i(tag: String, msg: String) { lines.add("I $msg") }'
  echo '    fun w(tag: String, msg: String) { lines.add("W $msg") }'
  echo "}"
  echo ""
  echo "class Scanner {"
  echo '    val ScanTag = "XENO-Scan"'
  echo "    val EBOOT_PATHS = listOf("
  echo '        "EBOOT.BIN",'
  echo '        "USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN",'
  echo '        "USRDIR/ISO.BIN.EDAT",'
  echo '        "PS3_GAME/USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN",'
  echo "    )"
  sed -n "${S1},${E1}p" "$SRC" \
    | sed -e 's/android\.util\.Log\.\(i\|w\)(/ScanLog.\1(/g' \
          -e 's/^    private fun /    fun /'
  echo "}"
  echo ""
  sed -n "${S2},${E2}p" "$SRC"
} > "$OUT"

echo "wrote $OUT (from $SRC:$S1-$E1, $S2-$E2)"

cd /home/runner/hub-work/xeno/code && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(android): list only folders the emulator can actually boot

The library listed any folder that had a PS3 title's SHAPE -- a PARAM.SFO
somewhere, USRDIR beside it, CATEGORY other than GD -- which is not the same
thing as a game. A shared folder is full of folders that pass that test and
cannot be played: PS3 homebrew is several titles apiece, so Cheat Engine alone
lands as CEFramework / CEHtmlApi / CEHtmlUI / CEPhWeb, next to log directories
and PS1 ROM sets and every other app's leftovers.

Every one of those is also a tile that can only fail. _rpcsx_boot resolves a
directory through locateEbootPath and, finding nothing, hands the bare
directory to Emu.BootGame, which answers invalid_file_or_folder. So the junk
in the list and "Game failed to start: InvalidFileOrFolder" on tap are the
same bug, and the fix is the same fix.

The bar applied here is the one the core already applies in fetchGameInfo
(rpcsx-android.cpp): BOOTABLE set, a TITLE_ID, and an EBOOT the core can open.
hasBootableEboot mirrors locateEbootPath's four candidates, so the scanner and
the core cannot disagree about a folder. Listing less than the core can boot is
the failure that costs the most time: an unbootable tile reads as a broken
emulator rather than a folder that was never a game.

Two things deliberately do NOT become stricter:

  - An unreadable PARAM.SFO proves nothing, so a parse failure falls back to the
    old structural answer. A truncated SFO must not hide a real game.
  - No USRDIR requirement. locateEbootPath also accepts an EBOOT.BIN beside the
    SFO, so requiring USRDIR was a second, stricter rule that hid games the
    emulator boots perfectly well.

The SAF path gets the structural half for the same reason; CATEGORY and BOOTABLE
are not read there, because a document tree has no path to open the SFO with.

ScanSchemaVersion 8 -> 9: the cache holds the scan RESULT, so without the bump
every existing install keeps serving the junk and never rescans.

Also, on the launch side:
  - _rpcsx_boot logs a directory it could not resolve to an EBOOT, naming the
    folder and the four paths it tried. That case was completely silent, and it
    is the whole explanation for the error the user sees.
  - The failure toast now distinguishes the three causes behind
    InvalidFileOrFolder: a folder with no EBOOT, a file that cannot be read
    (grant All files access), and a file that is not a disc.

Verified against 22 fixtures driving the shipped isPs3GameFolder/ParamSfo
(extracted verbatim into a JVM harness): real installed games, JB rips, PSN
games and an EBOOT at the folder root all stay listed; no-EBOOT, BOOTABLE=0,
no-TITLE_ID, CATEGORY=GD and SFO-without-payload are all filtered; truncated
and zero-byte SFOs still fall back to being listed.
EOF
git log --oneline -3

67:      * FOLDER form lays its ICON0.PNG, PIC1.PNG and every DLC image out on shared storage,
68:      * where the scanner indexes them and they land in the camera roll. One Minecraft folder
69:      * accounted for 245 images, which was every image in the whole ROM tree.
70:      *
71:      * The marker goes at the ROM directory root the user configured, not inside a game
72:      * folder: it covers current and future folder games in one file, and it never puts a
73:      * stray file inside content the emulator mounts as a disc.
74:      *
75:      * Zero bytes and reversible, deleting it restores the old behaviour. Best effort, since
76:      * the ROM folder may be read-only or reached over SAF.
77:      */
78:     private fun shieldFromMediaScanner(directory: File) {
79:         runCatching {
80:             val marker = File(directory, ".nomedia")
81:             if (marker.exists()) return
82: 
83:             if (marker.createNewFile()) {
84:                 android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "wrote .nomedia in ${directory.absolutePath}")
85:                 // Adding the marker does not retroactively drop what MediaStore already
86:                 // indexed. Re-scanning the path is what makes the provider re-evaluate the
87:                 // subtree and forget it.
88:                 runCatching {
89:                     android.media.MediaScannerConnection.scanFile(
90:                         context, arrayOf(directory.absolutePath), null, null,
91:                     )
92:                 }
93:             }
94:         }
95:     }

103:      * Absolute paths of installed titles the core cannot decrypt without a licence.
104:      *
105:      * Asked of the CORE rather than worked out here. The flag comes from actually attempting
106:      * decrypt_self on the game's EBOOT (fetchGameInfo, rpcsx-android.cpp), which is the only
107:      * honest answer to "does this need a .rap". Checking PARAM.SFO's CONTENT_ID against
108:      * exdata instead -- the obvious pure-Kotlin shortcut -- would call every PSN title locked,
109:      * including the many whose EBOOT needs no licence at all.

112:      * /storage/emulated/0 and /data/media/0 are one directory under two names.

115:      */

117:         if (!RPCSX.initialized) return emptySet()

122:             RPCSX.instance.collectGameInfo(dir.absolutePath, -1)

124:         NativeGames.list()
125:             .filter { it.hasFlag(GameFlag.Locked) }
126:             .mapNotNull { game -> runCatching { File(game.info.path).canonicalPath }.getOrNull() }
127:             .toSet()
128:     }.getOrDefault(emptySet())

149:     fun loadCached(): CachedLibrary {
150:         val cachedKey = MainActivityRuntime.prefs.getString("gamesCacheKey", null)
151:             ?: MainActivityRuntime.prefs.getString("gamesCacheDir", null)
152:         val json = MainActivityRuntime.prefs.getString("gamesCache", null)
153:             ?: return CachedLibrary(cachedKey, emptyList())
154:         val games = runCatching {
155:             val array = JSONArray(json)
156:             buildList {
157:                 repeat(array.length()) { index ->
158:                     val item = array.getJSONObject(index)
159:                     add(
160:                         GameInfo(
161:                             uri = item.getString("uri").toUri(),
162:                             title = item.getString("title"),
163:                             serial = if (item.isNull("serial")) null else item.optString("serial").takeIf(String::isNotBlank),
164:                             compatibility = item.optInt("compat", 0),
165:                             extension = item.optString("ext").ifBlank {
166:                                 item.getString("uri").substringAfterLast('.', "").uppercase()
167:                             },
168:                             platform = GamePlatform.fromKey(item.optString("platform").takeIf(String::isNotBlank)),
169:                             // Absent in a cache written before #338 — optString gives "",
170:                             // which reads as "no separate sort key / not translated", so an
171:                             // old cache degrades to the previous behaviour until a rescan.
172:                             titleSort = item.optString("titleSort"),
173:                             titleEn = item.optString("titleEn"),
174:                             locked = item.optBoolean("locked", false),
175:                         ),
176:                     )
177:                 }
178:             }
179:         }.getOrDefault(emptyList())
180:         return CachedLibrary(cachedKey, games)
181:     }

183:     suspend fun scan(directories: List<String>): List<GameInfo> = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
184:         // Seed the probe cache from the last scan before touching anything.
185:         //
186:         // probeDisc mounts the image into the emulator's GLOBAL vfs to read its PARAM.SFO,
187:         // and discInfoCache only ever lived in memory on one repository instance, so every
188:         // rescan re-mounted every disc from scratch. That is slow on a 7 GB image and it is
189:         // the window in which a scan can collide with a boot or a teardown, which crashed
190:         // the process inside vfs::mount.
191:         //
192:         // Everything the probe produces is already durable: the serial and title are in the
193:         // library cache, and the icon is on disk under disc-icons. So a disc we have seen
194:         // before never needs mounting again.
195:         //
196:         // That last clause is only true if the extraction actually succeeded once. The serial
197:         // and title are durable by construction -- this loop is reading them -- but the icon
198:         // is a separate file that may never have been written: probeDiscInfo answers "{}"
199:         // whenever a game is loaded, and the serial then comes from the FILENAME instead,
200:         // which for dev_hdd0/game/<title id> is indistinguishable from one the SFO gave us.
201:         // Seeding on the serial alone made that miss permanent, because every later rescan
202:         // skipped the one thing that would repair it. Reported as a PKG-installed title
203:         // showing a text placeholder for good, with its ICON0.PNG sitting unread in the game
204:         // folder and its path already recorded in games.json.
205:         //
206:         // So gate the skip on the icon as well, for the games that have one. Re-probing costs
207:         // one mount, once, and only for a game actually missing it; a game whose icon is on
208:         // disk still never mounts again, which is what the reasoning above is protecting.
209:         loadCached().games.forEach { game ->
210:             val serial = game.serial?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() } ?: return@forEach
211:             val path = runCatching { game.uri.path }.getOrNull() ?: return@forEach
212:             // Folders only, and that is not a convenience: re-probing an ISO means load_iso ->
213:             // vfs::mount, which is the process-wide mount this whole seeding exists to avoid, and
214:             // it has crashed the app for real -- twice in one day, faulting in
215:             // manual_typemap::init<vfs_manager> from this very thread while a boot was starting.
216:             // A directory is read straight off disk by read_sfo_game_info with no mount at all,
217:             // so it carries none of that risk. The game this was reported for was a PKG install
218:             // (folder form) whose ICON0.PNG was sitting there unread, which is exactly the case
219:             // that stays covered.
220:             val isFolder = game.extension.equals("folder", ignoreCase = true)
221:             if (isFolder && !DiscIcons.has(serial)) {
222:                 android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "re-probing folder '$serial': no usable disc icon on disk")
223:                 return@forEach
224:             }
225:             discInfoCache.putIfAbsent(path, DiscInfo(serial, game.title))
226:         }
227: 
228:         val collected = linkedMapOf<String, GameInfo>()
229:         android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "scan start: ${directories.size} dir(s), rawStorage=${canUseRawStorage()}")
230:         directories.forEach { rawUri ->
231:             val uri = runCatching { rawUri.toUri() }.getOrNull() ?: return@forEach
232:             val posix = MainActivityRuntime.resolveTreeUriToPosix(rawUri)
233:             val rawRoot = if (canUseRawStorage()) posix?.let(::File) else null
234:             android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "dir=$rawUri -> posix=$posix isDir=${rawRoot?.isDirectory}")
235:             if (rawRoot?.isDirectory == true) {
236:                 shieldFromMediaScanner(rawRoot)
237:                 scanRawDirectory(rawRoot, collected, 0)
238:             } else {
239:                 // SAF fallback. Games found this way are LISTED but the core cannot boot them:
240:                 // it opens games with ordinary file IO and a document tree has no path to open.
241:                 // Without All files access every folder outside the emulator's own directory
242:                 // lands here, which reads as "the game is there but hangs on its loading
243:                 // screen" rather than as a permissions problem. Say which it is.
244:                 val tree = DocumentFile.fromTreeUri(context, uri)
245:                 if (!canUseRawStorage()) {
246:                     android.util.Log.w(
247:                         ScanTag,
248:                         "  $rawUri is being scanned over SAF because All files access is not " +
249:                             "granted. Games found here will appear in the library but cannot be " +
250:                             "read by the emulator -- grant the permission, or move them into " +
251:                             "the games directory inside the emulator folder."
252:                     )
253:                 } else {
254:                     android.util.Log.w(
255:                         ScanTag,
256:                         "  $rawUri has no filesystem path (posix=$posix); falling back to SAF. " +
257:                             "Games found here cannot be read by the emulator."
258:                     )
259:                 }
260:                 android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  SAF fallback: tree=${tree?.uri} canRead=${tree?.canRead()} children=${runCatching { tree?.listFiles()?.size }.getOrNull()}")
261:                 tree?.let { scanDocumentTree(it, collected, 0) }
262:             }
263:         }
264:         internalGameDirectories().forEach { dir ->
265:             android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "internal dir=${dir.absolutePath}")
266:             // dev_hdd0/game is the emulator's own install root and its shape is known: one
267:             // directory per title, nothing else. It gets the strict scan. Everything else is
268:             // a folder a user pointed us at, where games legitimately sit at any depth.
269:             if (dir.name == "game") scanInstalledTitles(dir, collected)
270:             else scanRawDirectory(dir, collected, 0)
271:         }
272:         val locked = lockedGamePaths()
273:         android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "scan done: ${collected.size} game(s), ${locked.size} locked")
274:         collected.values
275:             .map { game ->
276:                 val path = runCatching { game.uri.path?.let { File(it).canonicalPath } }.getOrNull()
277:                 if (path != null && path in locked) game.copy(locked = true) else game
278:             }
279:             .sortedBy { it.title.lowercase() }
280:             .also { saveCache(directories, it) }
281:     }

348:      * Mirrors the recently-played list to a plain `recent_games.json` under the app's data
349:      * root (the shared-storage folder the user picked, next to gamesettings/ and memcards/;
350:      * or the app-private externalFilesDir when none was chosen). `recentGameUris` lives in

355:      * (PR #391), reworked here to run off-thread and to also fire on removal.

357:     private fun exportRecentGamesPublic(orderedUris: List<String>, justPlayed: GameInfo? = null) {
358:         val root = MainActivityRuntime.systemDirPosix()
359:             ?: context.getExternalFilesDir(null)?.absolutePath
360:             ?: return
361:         val cached = loadCached().games
362:         val byUri = (if (justPlayed != null) cached + justPlayed else cached).associateBy { it.uri.toString() }

365:             val g = byUri[uriString] ?: return@forEach

367:                 put("uri", g.uri.toString())

369:                 put("serial", g.serial ?: JSONObject.NULL)

371:                 put("platform", g.platform.key)

379:     private fun scanDocumentTree(
380:         directory: DocumentFile,
381:         output: MutableMap<String, GameInfo>,
382:         depth: Int,
383:     ) {
384:         if (depth > MaxScanDepth) return
385:         val children = runCatching { directory.listFiles() }.getOrNull() ?: return
386:         children.forEach { file ->
387:             if (file.isDirectory) {
388:                 // Same leaf rule as the raw scan. No SFO probe here: the core opens
389:                 // by path and a content:// tree has none to give, so the title comes
390:                 // from the folder name -- as it already does for a SAF-listed .iso.
391:                 if (runCatching { isPs3GameDocument(file) }.getOrDefault(false)) {
392:                     output.putIfAbsent(
393:                         file.uri.toString(),
394:                         createGame(file.uri, file.name ?: "", "folder", null),
395:                     )
396:                     return@forEach
397:                 }
398:                 scanDocumentTree(file, output, depth + 1)
399:                 return@forEach
400:             }
401:             val name = file.name ?: return@forEach
402:             val extension = name.substringAfterLast('.', "").lowercase()
403:             if (extension !in gameExtensions) return@forEach
404:             val probe = if (extension in probeExtensions) probeDocument(file.uri) else null
405:             output.putIfAbsent(file.uri.toString(), createGame(file.uri, name, extension, probe))
406:         }
407:     }

409:     /**
410:      * True when this directory IS a game rather than a folder containing games.
411:      *
412:      * Two shapes, both common and neither an .iso:
413:      *   - a JB folder dump, which keeps the disc layout: <dir>/PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO
414:      *     (PS3_DISC.SFB alongside it on a real disc rip)
415:      *   - an installed/HDD game folder -- PARAM.SFO next to USRDIR. This is what
416:      *     RPCS3's own games directory holds, and the shape prototypes that never
417:      *     got a retail master ship in.
418:      *
419:      * Case-insensitive: these come off FAT/exFAT cards and out of archives, so
420:      * "PS3_GAME" is as likely to be "ps3_game".
421:      */
422:     private fun isPs3GameFolder(directory: File): Boolean {
423:         fun child(vararg path: String): File? {
424:             var current: File = directory
425:             for (segment in path) {
426:                 current = current.listFiles()
427:                     ?.firstOrNull { it.name.equals(segment, ignoreCase = true) }
428:                     ?: return null
429:             }
430:             return current
431:         }
432:         if (child("PS3_GAME", "PARAM.SFO")?.isFile == true) return true
433:         if (child("PS3_DISC.SFB")?.isFile == true) return true
434:         val sfo = child("PARAM.SFO")?.takeIf { it.isFile } ?: return false
435:         if (child("USRDIR")?.isDirectory != true) return false
436:         // A game data install has this exact shape too, a PARAM.SFO next to USRDIR, so the
437:         // layout alone cannot tell it apart from an HDD game. It holds no EBOOT, so listing it
438:         // gave every title that installs data a second tile that cannot boot (Skate 3's 1.1 GB
439:         // BLUS30464_INSTALL, sitting next to the disc it belongs to). CATEGORY is what
440:         // separates them: GD is data, HG and DG are games. The native scanner already rejects
441:         // these because fetchGameInfo requires BOOTABLE and game data does not set it. This
442:         // applies the same rule to the folder path, which never opens the SFO at all.
443:         return sfoCategory(sfo) != "GD"
444:     }
445: 
446:     /**
447:      * CATEGORY out of a PARAM.SFO, or null when it cannot be read.
448:      *
449:      * A malformed or truncated file has to degrade to "list it" rather than hide a real game,
450:      * which is what [ParamSfo] answering null for every failure buys here.
451:      */
452:     private fun sfoCategory(sfo: File): String? = ParamSfo.string(sfo, "CATEGORY")
453: 
454:     /** [isPs3GameFolder] over a SAF tree. */
455:     private fun isPs3GameDocument(directory: DocumentFile): Boolean {
456:         val children = runCatching { directory.listFiles() }.getOrNull() ?: return false
457:         fun find(name: String) = children.firstOrNull { it.name.equals(name, ignoreCase = true) }
458:         if (find("PS3_DISC.SFB")?.isFile == true) return true
459:         find("PS3_GAME")?.takeIf { it.isDirectory }?.let { gameDir ->
460:             val inner = runCatching { gameDir.listFiles() }.getOrNull().orEmpty()
461:             if (inner.any { it.isFile && it.name.equals("PARAM.SFO", ignoreCase = true) }) return true
462:         }
463:         return find("PARAM.SFO")?.isFile == true && find("USRDIR")?.isDirectory == true
464:     }

466:     /**
467:      * dev_hdd0/game, scanned as what it is: one directory per installed title.
468:      *
469:      * The recursive scan cannot be used here. It descends into anything that is not itself a
470:      * game folder and then accepts any file whose extension is in [gameExtensions], and "img"
471:      * is one of those. A title's own data is full of them, so once a package unpacked its
472:      * contents over this directory rather than into a title folder of its own, GTA IV's
473:      * archives arrived in the library as games: manhat01, props_ab, vehicles, script,
474:      * weapons. Every one of them a .img sitting where the scanner was willing to look.
475:      *
476:      * The extractor no longer unpacks into this directory (see unpkg.cpp set_install_path),
477:      * but nothing should be relying on that to keep the library clean, and existing installs
478:      * still have the debris. A direct child here is a title or it is not listed.
479:      */
480:     private fun scanInstalledTitles(directory: File, output: MutableMap<String, GameInfo>) {
481:         val children = runCatching { directory.listFiles() }.getOrNull() ?: return
482:         children.forEach { file ->
483:             if (!file.isDirectory) return@forEach
484:             if (!runCatching { isPs3GameFolder(file) }.getOrDefault(false)) {
485:                 android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  skipping non-title '${file.name}' in dev_hdd0/game")
486:                 return@forEach
487:             }
488:             val uri = Uri.fromFile(file)
489:             android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  installed title '${file.name}'")
490:             output.putIfAbsent(
491:                 uri.toString(),
492:                 createGame(uri, file.name, "folder", null, probeDisc(file)),
493:             )
494:         }
495:     }

497:     private fun scanRawDirectory(
498:         directory: File,
499:         output: MutableMap<String, GameInfo>,
500:         depth: Int,
501:     ) {
502:         if (depth > MaxScanDepth) return
503:         val children = runCatching { directory.listFiles() }.getOrNull() ?: return
504:         children.forEach { file ->
505:             if (file.isDirectory) {
506:                 // A game folder is a leaf: emit it and do NOT descend. Descending
507:                 // also used to add USRDIR/EBOOT.BIN as its own bogus entry, since
508:                 // "bin" is in gameExtensions.
509:                 if (runCatching { isPs3GameFolder(file) }.getOrDefault(false)) {
510:                     val folderUri = Uri.fromFile(file)
511:                     android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  game folder '${file.name}'")
512:                     output.putIfAbsent(
513:                         folderUri.toString(),
514:                         createGame(folderUri, file.name, "folder", null, probeDisc(file)),
515:                     )
516:                     return@forEach
517:                 }
518:                 scanRawDirectory(file, output, depth + 1)
519:                 return@forEach
520:             }
521:             val extension = file.extension.lowercase()
522:             android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  raw file '${file.name}' ext=$extension accepted=${extension in gameExtensions}")
523:             if (extension !in gameExtensions) return@forEach
524:             val uri = Uri.fromFile(file)
525:             val disc = if (extension in probeExtensions) probeDisc(file) else null
526:             val probe = if (disc == null && extension in probeExtensions) probeRaw(file) else null
527:             output.putIfAbsent(uri.toString(), createGame(uri, file.name, extension, probe, disc))
528:         }
529:     }
