531:     /**
532:      * Drop the separator, but only from something that actually looks like a title ID.
533:      *
534:      * The check is not about which console the game is for -- this emulator runs PS3 titles
535:      * and nothing else. It is about not manufacturing an identity out of a guess.
536:      * FilenameParser takes the first four-letters + five-digits token it finds ANYWHERE in
537:      * the name and reconstructs it in the PS2 dump shape it was written for, so what arrives
538:      * here may be a real id (BLUS-30917), a token out of a release tag, or an id belonging to
539:      * a different game entirely.
540:      *
541:      * Left hyphenated, a bad guess matches nothing: no cover, no disc icon, no config, and
542:      * the card shows a placeholder. That is a visible failure and it is the safe one.
543:      * Stripped, the same guess becomes a WELL-FORMED title id and quietly resolves whatever
544:      * is filed under it -- another game's cover and curated name, and its config_db entry,
545:      * which the core applies at boot. So normalise only what carries a real PS3 prefix:
546:      * B for disc releases (BLUS/BLES/BCUS...), N for PSN (NPUB/NPEB...).
547:      *
548:      * Deliberately NOT gated on [GamePlatform]: that enum comes from the same probe that
549:      * produced the serial, so in the one case this function exists for -- the probe failed
550:      * and the name came off the filename -- it carries no information at all.
551:      */

582:                             is Long -> putLong(key.replace(old, new), value)

651:     /** GameDB's three titles for [serial], or null when it isn't in the database. */

663:     private fun parseProbe(value: String?): Pair<String?, GamePlatform?> {

670:     private fun probeDocument(uri: Uri): String? = runCatching {
671:         val descriptor = context.contentResolver.openFileDescriptor(uri, "r") ?: return null

675:     private fun probeRaw(file: File): String? = runCatching {

680:     /**
681:      * Read a PS3 disc's title ID, title and cover from the image itself.
682:      *

684:      * with no serial -- and no serial meant no title, no compatibility entry and

686:      * extracting PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG alongside it.

692:      */

696:         val existing = discInfoCache[file.absolutePath]
697:         if (existing != null) return existing

699:         val raw = runCatching {
700:             RPCSX.instance.probeDiscInfo(file.absolutePath, DiscIcons.fileFor(PendingIcon).absolutePath)

702:         android.util.Log.i(ScanTag, "  probeDiscInfo('${file.name}') -> $raw")

706:             val o = JSONObject(raw)

708:             if (id.isBlank()) return@runCatching null

781:          *  v6: PARAM.SFO CATEGORY read, to drop game-data installs.
782:          *  v7: licence-locked state, asked of the core per installed title.
783:          *  v8: PS3 serials normalised (BLUS-30917 -> BLUS30917). The scanner does not
784:          *      extract a NEW field here, it changes the VALUE of one it already stored, which
785:          *      has the same staleness signature: without a bump an existing install keeps
786:          *      serving the cached hyphenated ids and never rescans, so the repair never
787:          *      reaches the libraries that need it. */
788:         /** PS3 disc ids are B***, PSN ids N***, both four letters and five digits. */
789:         val ps3SerialRegex = Regex("^[BN][A-Z]{3}[0-9]{5}$")
790: 
791:         const val ScanSchemaVersion = 8
792:         const val ScanTag = "XENO-Scan"

794:         const val PendingIcon = "__pending"
795:         const val MaxScanDepth = 12
796:         val probeExtensions = setOf("iso", "bin", "chd", "img", "mdf", "nrg", "dump")
797:     }
798: }

800: /**
801:  * The one PARAM.SFO field a caller asks for, by key.
802:  *
803:  * Grown out of the scanner's CATEGORY reader rather than added beside it: the package screen
804:  * needs TITLE for the same files, and a second copy of this parsing would be a second place to
805:  * get the 16-byte index-entry layout wrong.
806:  *
807:  * Every failure -- unreadable file, wrong magic, an offset that points past the end -- answers
808:  * null. A truncated or hand-edited SFO must never take a caller down with it: the scanner uses
809:  * the answer to decide whether to LIST a game, and the package screen to decide what to CALL
810:  * one, and both have a sane fallback while an exception has none.
811:  */
812: internal object ParamSfo {
813:     fun string(sfo: File, key: String): String? =
814:         runCatching { string(sfo.readBytes(), key) }.getOrNull()
815: 
816:     fun string(bytes: ByteArray, key: String): String? {
817:         val buffer = java.nio.ByteBuffer.wrap(bytes).order(java.nio.ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN)
818:         // "\0PSF", then key-table start, data-table start, entry count.
819:         if (bytes.size < 20 || buffer.getInt(0) != 0x46535000) return null
820:         val keyTable = buffer.getInt(8)
821:         val dataTable = buffer.getInt(12)
822:         for (index in 0 until buffer.getInt(16)) {
823:             val entry = 20 + index * 16
824:             if (entry + 16 > bytes.size) break
825:             val keyStart = keyTable + (buffer.getShort(entry).toInt() and 0xFFFF)
826:             if (keyStart < 0 || keyStart >= bytes.size) break
827:             var keyEnd = keyStart
828:             while (keyEnd < bytes.size && bytes[keyEnd] != 0.toByte()) keyEnd++
829:             if (String(bytes, keyStart, keyEnd - keyStart) != key) continue
830:             val dataStart = dataTable + buffer.getInt(entry + 12)
831:             val dataLength = buffer.getInt(entry + 4)
832:             if (dataStart < 0 || dataLength < 0 || dataStart + dataLength > bytes.size) break
833:             // Values are UTF-8 and padded with NULs to their declared maximum length.
834:             return String(bytes, dataStart, dataLength, Charsets.UTF_8).trimEnd('\u0000', ' ')
835:         }
836:         return null
837:     }
838: }

375: data class GameInfo(
376:     val uri: Uri,
377:     val title: String,
378:     val serial: String?,
379:     val compatibility: Int = 0,    // 0..5 (TODO: pull from gamedb)
380:     val extension: String = "",    // upper-case container ext, e.g. "ISO", "CHD"
381:     val platform: GamePlatform = GamePlatform.PS2,
382:     /** GameDB `name-sort` — the title's sort key. For a Japanese game this is the kana
383:      *  reading, which is the only way the list sorts the way a Japanese reader expects:
384:      *  sorting the kanji sorts by codepoint, which is meaningless. Empty when the DB has
385:      *  no separate key (most non-JP games), or when the title came from the filename. */
386:     val titleSort: String = "",
387:     /** GameDB `name-en` — the romanised title, present only where the original isn't
388:      *  English. Its presence is exactly how we know [title] is non-English. */
389:     val titleEn: String = "",
390:     /** The core could not decrypt this title's EBOOT, so it needs a .rap licence before it
391:      *  will boot. Only ever set for games in the emulator's own storage, since that is where
392:      *  a PKG install puts them and the only place the core is asked about. */
393:     val locked: Boolean = false,
394: ) {
395:     /** The title to show. Mirrors GameList.h's `GetTitle(force_en)`: the original unless
396:      *  English is asked for AND a separate English title exists. */
397:     /** A user override wins over both the parsed and the English title — it exists precisely
398:      *  because those are wrong for this disc (see [CustomNames]). */
399:     fun displayTitle(forceEn: Boolean): String =
400:         CustomNames.nameFor(settingsKey)
401:             ?: if (forceEn && titleEn.isNotEmpty()) titleEn else title
402: 
403:     /** The key to sort by. Mirrors GameList.h's `GetTitleSort(force_en)`, including the
404:      *  subtlety it documents: when a separate English title exists, [titleSort] is in the
405:      *  WRONG language for an English list, so the English title has to sort itself. */
406:     fun sortKey(forceEn: Boolean): String = when {
407:         // A renamed game sorts under the name the user actually sees; otherwise it files
408:         // itself under the garbage title they renamed it to get away from ("UN6 A35" landing
409:         // under U instead of N for Naruto).
410:         !CustomNames.nameFor(settingsKey).isNullOrBlank() -> CustomNames.nameFor(settingsKey)!!
411:         forceEn && titleEn.isNotEmpty() -> titleEn
412:         titleSort.isNotEmpty() -> titleSort
413:         else -> title
414:     }
415:     /**
416:      * What the UI hands Coil. A local disc icon when we extracted one, otherwise
417:      * the remote cover URL.
418:      *
419:      * Kept separate from [coverUrl] rather than widening its type: Discord rich
420:      * presence needs a real URL it can fetch, and a File would silently become a
421:      * useless path string there.
422:      */
423:     val coverModel: Any? get() = coverUrl ?: discIconFile
424: 
425:     val coverUrl: String? get() = serial?.let { rawSerial ->
426:         // Cover Region: swap in the equivalent release's serial when the user asked for another
427:         // region's artwork. Falls back to this disc's own serial whenever there's no counterpart,
428:         // so an unmatched game looks exactly as it does today.
429:         coverUrlFor(CoverRegionIndex.coverSerialFor(rawSerial) ?: rawSerial)
430:     }
431: 
432:     /** This disc's OWN cover, ignoring the Cover Region choice. The card falls back to it when the
433:      *  regional cover 404s — not every game has art for every region in the cover repo, and losing
434:      *  a cover you previously had is worse than simply not getting the regional one. */
435:     val discCoverUrl: String? get() = serial?.let { coverUrlFor(it) }
436: 
437:     /**
438:      * PS3 cover art comes off the DISC, not a repo.
439:      *
440:      * Every PS3 disc carries PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG -- the artwork the console
441:      * itself shows on the XMB, and what desktop RPCS3 shows in its game grid.
442:      * The scanner extracts it once per game, so covers need no network, never
443:      * 404, and always match the disc. There is no PS3 equivalent of xlenore's
444:      * ps2-covers to point at anyway.
445:      */
446:     // Length rather than isFile, for the same reason as DiscIcons.has: an empty file passes
447:     // isFile, hands Coil something undecodable, and costs the card its placeholder-vs-cover
448:     // decision. Nothing is a better answer than zero bytes.
449:     val discIconFile: java.io.File? get() = serial?.let { DiscIcons.fileFor(it) }?.takeIf { it.length() > 0L }
450: 
451:     private fun coverUrlFor(s: String): String {
452:         // PS3 art comes from aldostools/Resources, which is flat: COV/<TITLE_ID>.JPG
453:         // keyed by exactly the id PARAM.SFO gives us. Extension is UPPER-case there
454:         // -- the lower-case URL 404s. No 3D/spine set exists, so the 3D toggle has
455:         // nothing to switch to and this ignores it.
456:         if (platform == GamePlatform.PS3) {
457:             return "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aldostools/Resources/main/COV/$s.JPG"
458:         }
459:         val repo = when (platform) {
460:             GamePlatform.PS2 -> "ps2-covers"
461:             GamePlatform.PS1 -> "psx-covers"
462:             GamePlatform.PS3 -> "ps2-covers"  // handled above
463:         }
464:         // 3D cases live under covers/3d/*.png; flat 2D scans under
465:         // covers/default/*.jpg. Coil decodes by content, so the extension
466:         // mismatch on the cached file is fine.
467:         return if (CoverArtStyle.use3d.value)
468:             "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xlenore/$repo/main/covers/3d/$s.png"
469:         else
470:             "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xlenore/$repo/main/covers/default/$s.jpg"
471:     }
472: 
473:     /** Human-readable region (USA / Europe / Japan / India / China / …). Prefers the
474:      *  curated GameDB region (so India/China/Korea/HK releases that share a serial PREFIX
475:      *  with Europe/Japan are labelled correctly — matching PCSX2), falling back to the
476:      *  serial-prefix heuristic when the serial isn't in the database. Shown under the
477:      *  cover so users can tell apart multiple regional versions of the same game. */
478:     val region: String? get() = serial?.let { gameDbRegion(it) ?: regionForSerial(it) }
479: 
480:     /** Region as a flag emoji (🇺🇸 / 🇪🇺 / 🇯🇵 / …) for the cover label, or null.
481:      *  Rendered ahead of the title so the region is always visible even when a
482:      *  long name wraps/ellipsizes. */
483:     val regionFlag: String? get() = region?.let { regionFlagFor(it) }
484: 
485:     /** A short version/edition tag shown under the title so two copies of the
486:      *  same game can be told apart: a disc-version token parsed from the dump
487:      *  filename (e.g. "v3.00") when present, otherwise the serial. */
488:     val versionTag: String? get() {
489:         val name = uri.lastPathSegment?.substringAfterLast('/')?.substringAfterLast(':')
490:         return name?.let { FilenameParser.versionTokenOf(it) } ?: serial
491:     }
492: 
493:     /** Stable per-game identity used to key per-game SETTINGS (config.game.<key>).
494:      *  Disc games use their serial (byte-identical to before). Serial-less
495:      *  ELF/homebrew fall back to a normalized filename stem so their per-game
496:      *  settings persist across a reboot — a serial-keyed store silently dropped
497:      *  them to global at boot, which is issue #253. Derived purely from the ROM
498:      *  path so the boot path and the in-game overlay resolve the SAME key (the
499:      *  bug was the overlay saving under one key while boot read another). Stem
500:      *  keys can collide if two ELFs share a filename; acceptable for homebrew. */
501:     val settingsKey: String? get() = serial?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
502:         ?: uri.lastPathSegment?.substringAfterLast('/')?.substringAfterLast(':')
503:             ?.substringBeforeLast('.')?.trim()?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
504: }
505: 
506: /**
507:  * User-supplied cover overrides for games the online repo can't match — homebrew,
508:  * ELF ports, obscure dumps with no serial. Stored as image files under
509:  * `<dataRoot>/covers/custom/`. A cover is matched case-insensitively (png / jpg /
510:  * jpeg / webp) by the game's serial, its ROM filename, OR its displayed title — so
511:  * dropping in a file named after the game just works, and the in-app picker writes
512:  * to the same folder. A custom cover always wins over the online repo cover.
513:  */
514: object CustomCovers {
515:     /** Bumped on set/remove so cover tiles re-resolve. */
516:     val version = mutableStateOf(0)
517: 
518:     // MainActivityRuntime.assetCopyRoot() can flip between the chosen system dir and the
519:     // app-private fallback depending on a transient write-probe — so covers got
520:     // stored under one root and looked up under another ("sometimes there,
521:     // sometimes not"). Cache the covers root on first resolve so set + load always
522:     // agree, and share this exact cache with the library cover loader.
523:     @Volatile
524:     private var cachedCoversRoot: File? = null
525:     fun coversRoot(context: Context): File =
526:         cachedCoversRoot ?: File(MainActivityRuntime.assetCopyRoot(context), "covers").also { cachedCoversRoot = it }
527: 
528:     private fun dir(context: Context): File = File(coversRoot(context), "custom")
529: 
530:     private fun filenameStem(game: GameInfo): String? =
531:         game.uri.lastPathSegment?.substringAfterLast('/')?.substringAfterLast(':')
532:             ?.substringBeforeLast('.')?.trim()?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
533: 
534:     /** Names the user might give the cover file, highest priority first. */
535:     private fun keys(game: GameInfo): List<String> = buildList {
536:         game.serial?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }?.let { add(it) }
537:         filenameStem(game)?.let { add(it) }
538:         game.title.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }?.let { add(it) }
539:     }
540: 
541:     /** Load all custom covers as lowercased-stem -> File, in ONE directory
542:      *  listing. The library preloads this once (and refreshes on [version]) so
543:      *  cover tiles can resolve synchronously instead of each doing its own I/O
544:      *  during a scroll — which raced and mis-assigned covers across games. */
545:     fun loadAll(context: Context): Map<String, File> {
546:         val files = dir(context).listFiles()?.filter { it.isFile && it.length() > 0L } ?: return emptyMap()
547:         if (files.isEmpty()) return emptyMap()
548:         val byStem = HashMap<String, File>(files.size)
549:         for (f in files) byStem.putIfAbsent(f.nameWithoutExtension.lowercase(), f)
550:         return byStem
551:     }
552: 
553:     /** Resolve [game]'s cover against a preloaded [loadAll] map. No I/O.
554:      *  Look-up keys are run through the same [sanitize] the writer uses, so a
555:      *  title containing : / \ etc. (which [targetFor] wrote as '_') still
556:      *  resolves; sanitize is a no-op for clean keys. */
557:     fun matchIn(map: Map<String, File>, game: GameInfo): File? {
558:         if (map.isEmpty()) return null
559:         for (k in keys(game)) map[sanitize(k).lowercase()]?.let { return it }
560:         return null
561:     }
562: 
563:     /** An existing custom cover for [game], or null. Single-game convenience
564:      *  (does its own listing) — used off the scroll path. */
565:     fun fileFor(context: Context, game: GameInfo): File? = matchIn(loadAll(context), game)
566: 
567:     /** Path the in-app picker writes to (serial if present, else ROM filename). */
568:     private fun targetFor(context: Context, game: GameInfo): File {
569:         val key = game.serial?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
570:             ?: filenameStem(game) ?: game.title.ifBlank { "cover" }
571:         return File(dir(context), sanitize(key) + ".png")
572:     }
573: 
574:     /** Copy [source] in as [game]'s cover, replacing any prior one. */
575:     fun set(context: Context, game: GameInfo, source: Uri): Boolean = runCatching {
576:         remove(context, game)
577:         val target = targetFor(context, game)
578:         target.parentFile?.mkdirs()
579:         context.contentResolver.openInputStream(source)?.use { ins ->
580:             target.outputStream().use { outs -> ins.copyTo(outs) }
581:         }
582:         (target.isFile && target.length() > 0L).also { if (it) version.value++ }
583:     }.getOrDefault(false)
584: 
585:     /**
586:      * Follow a game's custom cover across an identity correction.
587:      *
588:      * The file is named after the serial, so a game whose id is corrected stops matching its
589:      * own cover -- and because [remove] resolves through the same name, the orphan cannot be
590:      * deleted from the app either. Skips when a cover already exists under the new id, so a
591:      * deliberate choice is never overwritten by a stale one.
592:      */
593:     fun renameSerial(context: Context, old: String, new: String): Boolean = runCatching {
594:         val from = File(dir(context), sanitize(old) + ".png")
595:         val to = File(dir(context), sanitize(new) + ".png")
596:         if (!from.isFile || to.exists()) return@runCatching false
597:         from.renameTo(to).also { if (it) version.value++ }
598:     }.getOrDefault(false)
599: 
600:     fun remove(context: Context, game: GameInfo): Boolean {
601:         val f = fileFor(context, game) ?: return false
602:         return f.delete().also { if (it) version.value++ }
603:     }
604: 
605:     private fun sanitize(s: String): String =
606:         s.replace(Regex("""[/\\:*?"<>|\n\r\t]"""), "_").trim().ifEmpty { "cover" }
607: }
608: 
609: /** Map a PS1/PS2 serial prefix to a region label. */
610: // GameDB region cache (serial -> mapped label, or "" = looked up & not in DB / no JNI).
611: // One native lookup per serial, then memoized so the cover/flag render path stays cheap
612: // during scroll. The GameDatabase is loaded by the time the library shows (the compat
613: // stars use it too), so this resolves for listed games.
614: private val gameDbRegionCache = java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap<String, String>()
615: 
616: /** The mapped region label from PCSX2's GameDB (India / China / Korea / Hong Kong / …),
617:  *  or null when the serial isn't in the database — the caller then falls back to the
618:  *  serial-prefix heuristic. Matches PCSX2, which a serial PREFIX can't (SCES = both
619:  *  Europe AND India, etc.). */
620: fun gameDbRegion(serial: String): String? {
621:     val cached = gameDbRegionCache.getOrPut(serial) {
622:         val raw = runCatching { com.xeno.NativeApp.getRegionForSerial(serial) }
623:             .getOrNull().orEmpty()
624:         mapGameDbRegion(raw) ?: ""
625:     }
626:     return cached.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
627: }
628: 
629: /** Map a PCSX2 GameDB region string ("NTSC-U", "PAL-E", "PAL-IN", "NTSC-C", "NTSC-HK", …)
630:  *  to our display label. */
631: private fun mapGameDbRegion(raw: String): String? {
632:     val u = raw.trim().uppercase()
633:     if (u.isEmpty()) return null
634:     return when {
635:         u == "PAL-IN" || u.contains("INDIA") -> "India"
636:         u.startsWith("NTSC-U") -> "USA"
637:         u.startsWith("NTSC-J") -> "Japan"
638:         u.startsWith("NTSC-K") -> "Korea"
639:         u.startsWith("NTSC-HK") -> "Hong Kong"
640:         u.startsWith("NTSC-C") -> "China"          // NTSC-C, NTSC-C-E, NTSC-C-J
641:         u.startsWith("NTSC-A") || u == "NTSC" -> "Asia"
642:         u.startsWith("PAL") -> "Europe"            // PAL, PAL-E, PAL-A, … (PAL-IN handled above)
643:         else -> null
644:     }
645: }
646: 
647: fun regionForSerial(serial: String): String? = when (serial.take(4).uppercase()) {
648:     "SLUS", "SCUS", "PBPX", "LSP0" -> "USA"
649:     "SLES", "SCES", "SLED", "SCED", "SLPN" -> "Europe"
650:     "SLPS", "SLPM", "SCPS", "SCAJ", "ALCH", "PAPX", "ROSE", "TCPS", "KOEI", "PCPX", "CPCS" -> "Japan"
651:     "SLKA", "SCKA" -> "Korea"
652:     "SLAJ" -> "Asia"
653:     else -> null
654: }
655: 
656: /** Map a region label to a flag emoji. Asia falls back to a globe. */
657: fun regionFlagFor(region: String): String? = when (region) {
658:     "USA" -> "🇺🇸"
659:     "Europe" -> "🇪🇺"
660:     "Japan" -> "🇯🇵"
661:     "Korea" -> "🇰🇷"
662:     "India" -> "🇮🇳"
663:     "China" -> "🇨🇳"
664:     "Hong Kong" -> "🇭🇰"
665:     "Asia" -> "🌏"
666:     else -> null
667: }

669: /**
670:  * Best-effort serial extractor. Recognized dump conventions:
671:  *   "Game (USA) [SLUS-20312].iso"      → SLUS-20312
672:  *   "Game (USA) [SLUS_203.12].iso"     → SLUS-20312
673:  *   "SCUS_972.28 - Game.iso"           → SCUS-97228
674:  *   "slus_203.12.iso"                  → SLUS-20312
675:  *
676:  * The pattern matches 4 letters + optional separator + 3 digits + optional
677:  * dot + 2 digits, normalized to "AAAA-NNNNN" upper-case.
678:  */
679: object FilenameParser {
680:     private val serialRegex = Regex("""([A-Za-z]{4})[\s_-]?(\d{3})\.?(\d{2})""")
681:     private val tagsRegex = Regex("""[\[(].*?[\])]""")
682:     // Disc-version token (e.g. "v3.00", "v 1.0"). The 'v' prefix is required so
683:     // release years ("(2004)") and unrelated x.y numbers aren't mistaken for it.
684:     private val versionRegex = Regex("""(?i)\bv\.?\s?(\d{1,2}(?:\.\d{1,2}){1,2})\b""")
685: 
686:     /** A disc-version token like "v3.00" parsed from a filename, or null. Lets
687:      *  two copies of the same game (same serial, different disc revision) be told
688:      *  apart when the dump filename carries the version. */
689:     fun versionTokenOf(filename: String): String? =
690:         versionRegex.find(filename)?.let { "v" + it.groupValues[1] }
691:     private val whitespaceRegex = Regex("""\s+""")
692:     private val nonWordRegex = Regex("""[^a-z0-9]+""")
693: 
694:     private data class FilenameAlias(val title: String, val serial: String)
695: 
696:     private fun aliasFor(filenameWithoutExt: String): FilenameAlias? {
697:         val normalized = filenameWithoutExt
698:             .lowercase()
699:             .replace(nonWordRegex, " ")
700:             .trim()
701: 
702:         // Some PAL DMC2 CHDs are named by disc character rather than serial,
703:         // and their raw-CD layout can be awkward to probe. Keep this narrow so
704:         // broader filename-only games still rely on explicit serial tokens.
705:         if (!normalized.contains("devil may cry 2"))
706:             return null
707: 
708:         return when {
709:             normalized.contains("dante") ->
710:                 FilenameAlias("Devil May Cry 2 [Dante Disc]", "SLES-82011")
711:             normalized.contains("lucia") ->
712:                 FilenameAlias("Devil May Cry 2 [Lucia Disc]", "SLES-82012")
713:             else -> null
714:         }
715:     }
716: 
717:     fun parse(filename: String): Pair<String, String?> {
718:         val withoutExt = filename.substringBeforeLast('.')
719:         val match = serialRegex.find(withoutExt)
720:         val serial = match?.let {
721:             "${it.groupValues[1].uppercase()}-${it.groupValues[2]}${it.groupValues[3]}"
722:         }
723:         if (serial == null) {
724:             aliasFor(withoutExt)?.let { return it.title to it.serial }
725:         }
726:         // Strip the matched serial token + any [region] / (lang) tags so the
727:         // displayed title is the game name rather than the full filename.
728:         var title = withoutExt
729:         if (match != null) title = title.replace(match.value, "")
730:         title = title.replace(tagsRegex, "")
731:             .replace(whitespaceRegex, " ")
732:             .trim(' ', '-', '_', '.')
733:         if (title.isEmpty()) title = withoutExt
734:         return title to serial
735:     }

13:  * package - 134 native methods belonging to a THIRD-PARTY rights holder, and
14:  * bound to PCSX2 besides. We do not copy that. This class re-declares the same
15:  * functional surface and implements it against RPCS3 instead, so the XENO UI
16:  * runs unchanged apart from its import line and nothing third-party crosses over.
17:  *
18:  * THREE KINDS OF METHOD LIVE HERE, and the distinction matters:
19:  *
20:  *   [MAPPED]      Backed by a real RPCS3 entry point. Works.
21:  *
22:  *   [PS3-N/A]     The concept does not exist on PS3 (PS2 memory cards, PNACH
23:  *                 patches, GUNCON lightguns, EE/VU speedhacks, RetroAchievements
24:  *                 - which has no PS3 support at all). These return a neutral
25:  *                 value AND the screen that drives them must be removed. A
26:  *                 control that silently does nothing is worse than an absent one.
27:  *
28:  *   [TODO]        Real PS3 analogue exists in RPCS3 but is not wired yet.
29:  *                 Distinguished from PS3-N/A on purpose: these are work items,
30:  *                 not dead ends.
31:  *
32:  * Every unimplemented method logs once via Unsupported.note() so a screen that
33:  * looks alive but is not shows up in logcat rather than being discovered by a
34:  * user.
35:  */

201:     /**
202:      * [TODO] Signature must match XENO's exactly - the UI passes all twelve
203:      * flags positionally, so a shorter overload silently fails to resolve at
204:      * every call site.
205:      *
206:      * RPCS3's equivalent is its Performance Overlay config node rather than
207:      * twelve independent booleans, so wiring this means mapping onto that.
208:      */
209:     public static void osdApplyFlags(boolean fps, boolean vps, boolean speed, boolean cpu,
210:                                      boolean gpu, boolean res, boolean gsStats,
211:                                      boolean frameTimes, boolean hwInfo, boolean version,
212:                                      boolean settings, boolean inputs) {
213:         // RPCS3 has no per-element toggles: one Enabled flag plus a detail_level
214:         // enum decides what appears. So collapse the twelve booleans onto that -
215:         // anything on means show the overlay, and the more the user asked for,
216:         // the higher the detail level.
217:         boolean any = fps || vps || speed || cpu || gpu || res || gsStats
218:             || frameTimes || hwInfo || version || settings || inputs;
219: 
220:         Rpcs3Settings.INSTANCE.setOverlayEnabled(any);
221:         if (!any) return;
222: 
223:         int count = 0;
224:         for (boolean b : new boolean[] { fps, vps, speed, cpu, gpu, res, gsStats,
225:                                          frameTimes, hwInfo, version, settings, inputs }) {
226:             if (b) count++;
227:         }
228: 
229:         String detail = count <= 1 ? "Minimal" : count <= 3 ? "Low"
230:                       : count <= 6 ? "Medium" : "High";
231:         Rpcs3Settings.INSTANCE.setOverlayDetail(detail);
232: 
233:         // These two ARE independent flags in RPCS3.
234:         Rpcs3Settings.INSTANCE.setOverlayFramerateGraph(fps);
235:         Rpcs3Settings.INSTANCE.setOverlayFrametimeGraph(frameTimes);
236:     }

263:     /**
264:      * [MAPPED] Custom Vulkan driver via adrenotools.
265:      *
266:      * The JNI glue opens the driver with adrenotools_open_libvulkan and hands
267:      * the resulting handle to the core, which points its Vulkan dispatch table
268:      * at it. Adreno only -- adrenotools patches Qualcomm's loader behaviour, and
269:      * supportsCustomVulkanDriver() probes /dev/kgsl-3d0 for exactly that.
270:      *
271:      * MUST be called before the renderer creates its VkInstance. Afterwards the
272:      * table is bound and swapping under a live device would invalidate every
273:      * object already created against the old driver.
274:      *
275:      * redirectDir is accepted for source compatibility with XENO's caller but
276:      * is not forwarded: ADRENOTOOLS_DRIVER_FILE_REDIRECT is not enabled here.
277:      */
278:     public static void setCustomVulkanDriver(String driverDir, String driverName,
279:                                              String redirectDir, String hookLibDir) {
280:         if (driverDir == null || driverDir.isEmpty()) {
281:             // Empty path clears the custom driver and reverts to the system one.
282:             net.rpcsx.RPCSX.Companion.getInstance().setCustomDriver("", "", "");
283:             android.util.Log.i("XENO-Driver", "reverted to the system Vulkan driver");
284:             return;
285:         }
286: 
287:         boolean ok = net.rpcsx.RPCSX.Companion.getInstance()
288:                 .setCustomDriver(driverDir, driverName, hookLibDir);
289:         if (ok) {
290:             android.util.Log.i("XENO-Driver", "custom Vulkan driver applied: " + driverName);
291:         } else {
292:             android.util.Log.e("XENO-Driver",
293:                     "custom Vulkan driver REJECTED: " + driverName + " in " + driverDir);
294:         }
295:     }
296: 
297:     /** Whether this device can load a user-supplied Vulkan driver (Adreno only). */
298:     public static boolean supportsCustomVulkanDriver() {
299:         try {
300:             return net.rpcsx.RPCSX.Companion.getInstance().supportsCustomDriverLoading();
301:         } catch (Throwable t) {
302:             return false;
303:         }
304:     }

372:      * RSX command volume and twice the GPU work, for frames no PS3 game was written to

380:      * get_display_refresh_rate() and uses it for Frame limit "Display"; it never wanted

@Composable
fun HomeScreen(
    onOpenMenu: () -> Unit,
    onOpenGameSettings: (GameInfo) -> Unit,
    modifier: Modifier = Modifier,
    viewModel: HomeViewModel = viewModel(),
) {
    val state = viewModel.state.value
    val directories = MainActivityRuntime.romsDirs.value
    val nativeReady = MainActivityRuntime.nativeReady.value
    val context = LocalContext.current
    val coverVersion = CustomCovers.version.value
    val customCoverMap = remember(coverVersion) { CustomCovers.loadAll(context) }
    var overflowMenu by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
    var showExitConfirm by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
    var menuGame by remember { mutableStateOf<GameInfo?>(null) }
    // Set by the context menu's "Install licence" entry; drives the .rap file browser.
    var licenceGame by remember { mutableStateOf<GameInfo?>(null) }
    // The game whose categories are being edited. Its own sheet rather than a submenu, because
    // filing a game usually means ticking more than one box.
    var categoriesGame by remember { mutableStateOf<GameInfo?>(null) }
    var categoryPicker by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
    // The category being renamed, if any. Long-press a row in the picker.
    var renameCategory by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
    var deleteCategory by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
    var showClearRecentsConfirm by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
    // #9 custom library background — inert until the user picks an image.
    LaunchedEffect(Unit) { LibraryBackground.ensureLoaded(); CoverArtStyle.load() }
    // The animated background switched itself off because the last run died with it on screen
    // (LibraryBackground.armSaver). Say so -- silently reverting a setting the user chose reads
    // as the setting being broken, and the name tells them which one to avoid.
    LaunchedEffect(LibraryBackground.crashedSaver.value) {
        LibraryBackground.crashedSaver.value?.let { kind ->
            LibraryBackground.crashedSaver.value = null
            Toast.makeText(
                context,
                "Animated background turned off: ${LibraryBackground.saverName(kind)} crashed last time.",
                Toast.LENGTH_LONG,
            ).show()
        }
    }
    val backgroundPicker = rememberLauncherForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.OpenDocument()) { picked ->
        picked?.let { LibraryBackground.set(context, it) }
    }
    // Search: both the controller (A on the Search zone) AND a touch tap open the app's own D-pad +
    // touch keyboard (LibraryKeyboard). The search bar is no longer an editable TextField, so the
    // Android system IME never appears. (Registered once the library has loaded.)
    val showSearch = LibraryChromePreferences.showSearch.value
    val showRecents = LibraryChromePreferences.showRecents.value
    val searchPlaceholder = str("games.search.placeholder")
    LaunchedEffect(state.initialized, showSearch) {
        if (!showSearch && viewModel.state.value.query.isNotEmpty()) viewModel.setQuery("")
        HomeInputController.setSearchAction(state.initialized && showSearch) {
            LibraryKeyboard.open(viewModel.state.value.query, viewModel::setQuery, searchPlaceholder)
        }
    }
    LaunchedEffect(directories, nativeReady) { viewModel.load(directories, nativeReady) }

package com.xeno

import java.io.File

/**
 * Cover art extracted from PS3 discs.
 *
 * XENO fetched covers from a GitHub repo keyed by serial. There is no
 * equivalent repo for the PS3, but there is something better: every disc
 * carries its own artwork at PS3_GAME/ICON0.PNG -- the image the console shows
 * on the XMB, and the one desktop RPCS3 shows in its game grid.
 *
 * The scanner extracts it once, on the pass that reads PARAM.SFO for the title
 * ID, so a cover costs nothing after the first scan: no network, no 404s, and
 * it always matches the disc it came from.
 *
 * Keyed by title ID (BLUS30464, BCES01234, ...), which is what PARAM.SFO gives
 * us and what everything else in the app already uses as the serial.
 */
object DiscIcons {

    private fun dir(): File =
        File(XenoApplication.appContext.filesDir, "disc-icons").apply { mkdirs() }

    fun fileFor(titleId: String): File = File(dir(), "$titleId.png")

    /**
     * True when this game's icon has already been extracted.
     *
     * Length, not isFile: an empty file is indistinguishable from a real one to isFile, and
     * it is a shape this can actually end up in -- the extraction writes to a staging name
     * and renames, and neither the write nor the rename is checked. An empty icon then reads
     * as "already extracted" forever, and the card falls through to the text placeholder
     * because there is nothing for Coil to decode. Requiring bytes makes that self-repairing:
     * the next scan re-probes and overwrites it.
     */
    fun has(titleId: String): Boolean = fileFor(titleId).length() > 0L

    fun clear() {
        runCatching { dir().listFiles()?.forEach { it.delete() } }
    }
}

# gl_compat.c answers the GL 1.x calls the sources make -- client-side vertex arrays, a
# fixed-function ortho and GL_QUADS -- with a GLES2 shader, so the renderer itself stays
# unmodified. See its header for what is and is not emulated.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_library(flurry SHARED
    flurry/flurry_jni.c
    flurry/gl_compat.c
    flurry/flurry.c
    flurry/flurry-smoke.c
    flurry/flurry-spark.c
    flurry/flurry-star.c
    flurry/flurry-texture.c
)

target_include_directories(flurry PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/flurry)
set_target_properties(flurry PROPERTIES C_STANDARD 99)

# -ffast-math: a particle simulation judged by eye, running thousands of sqrt per frame.
# Upstream shipped hand-written frsqrte paths for exactly this reason.
target_compile_options(flurry PRIVATE -O2 -ffast-math -Wall -Wno-unused-parameter)
target_link_libraries(flurry log GLESv2 m)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Really Slick Screensavers -> libsavers.so
#
# Terry Welsh's savers (GPL-2.0-or-later), compiled against a GLES2 shim rather than rewritten.
# The saver sources are BYTE-IDENTICAL to upstream: they are built with RS_XSCREENSAVER, which
# selects their platform-neutral path, and everything that path expects is answered by
# compat/. That keeps them re-pullable and keeps them recognisably his code.
#
# Separate from the flurry target because these are C++ and Flurry is C99, and because Flurry's
# shim is a different, smaller one. If a saver ever needs Flurry's, the two can merge.

add_library(savers SHARED
    savers/savers_jni.cpp
    savers/savers_platform.cpp
    savers/gl1.c

    # Each saver is compiled through a *_unit.cpp that wraps it in a namespace: they all
    # declare the same globals (draw, idleProc, cleanUp, readyToDraw) because each was built
    # as its own executable, and two in one .so collide at link time.
    savers/flux/flux_unit.cpp
    savers/flux/flux_port.cpp
    savers/plasma/plasma_unit.cpp
    savers/plasma/plasma_port.cpp
    savers/solarwinds/solarwinds_unit.cpp
    savers/solarwinds/solarwinds_port.cpp

    # Hyperspace. extensions.cpp is deliberately NOT built: it is the WIN32/GLX loader for the
    # ARB shader path, and the port takes the non-shader path instead. The entry points it
    # would have resolved are declared in compat/arb_shaders.h and defined in savers_platform.
    savers/hyperspace/unit_causticTextures.cpp
    savers/hyperspace/unit_flare.cpp
    savers/hyperspace/unit_goo.cpp
    savers/hyperspace/unit_hyperspace.cpp
    savers/hyperspace/unit_splinePath.cpp
    savers/hyperspace/unit_starBurst.cpp
    savers/hyperspace/unit_stretchedParticle.cpp
    savers/hyperspace/unit_tunnel.cpp
    savers/hyperspace/unit_wavyNormalCubeMaps.cpp
    savers/hyperspace/hyperspace_port.cpp

    savers/lattice/lattice_unit.cpp
    savers/lattice/lattice_port.cpp

    # Skyrocket. soundEngine.cpp is NOT built and its ~7MB of samples are not shipped: upstream
    # drives OpenAL, the port runs with dSound = 0, and soundEngine.h is a stub.
    savers/skyrocket/unit_flare.cpp
    savers/skyrocket/unit_particle.cpp
    savers/skyrocket/unit_shockwave.cpp
    savers/skyrocket/unit_skyrocket.cpp
    savers/skyrocket/unit_smoke.cpp
    savers/skyrocket/unit_world.cpp
    savers/skyrocket/skyrocket_port.cpp

    savers/rslibs/rsMath/rsVec.cpp
    savers/rslibs/rsMath/rsVec4.cpp
    savers/rslibs/rsMath/rsMatrix.cpp
    savers/rslibs/rsMath/rsQuat.cpp
    savers/rslibs/Rgbhsl/Rgbhsl.cpp

    # Implicit surfaces: Hyperspace's "goo" is a marching-cubes isosurface.
    savers/rslibs/Implicit/impSurface.cpp
    savers/rslibs/Implicit/impCubeVolume.cpp
    savers/rslibs/Implicit/impCubeTables.cpp
    savers/rslibs/Implicit/impShape.cpp
    savers/rslibs/Implicit/impSphere.cpp
    savers/rslibs/Implicit/impCapsule.cpp
    savers/rslibs/Implicit/impEllipsoid.cpp
    savers/rslibs/Implicit/impHexahedron.cpp
    savers/rslibs/Implicit/impRoundedHexahedron.cpp
    savers/rslibs/Implicit/impKnot.cpp
    savers/rslibs/Implicit/impTorus.cpp

)

target_include_directories(savers PRIVATE
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/savers
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/savers/compat
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/savers/rslibs
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/savers/flux
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/savers/plasma
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/savers/solarwinds
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/savers/hyperspace
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/savers/lattice
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/savers/skyrocket
)

# RS_XSCREENSAVER picks the savers' platform-neutral path. Without it they compile their Win32
# shell and nothing links.
target_compile_definitions(savers PRIVATE RS_XSCREENSAVER)
set_target_properties(savers PROPERTIES C_STANDARD 99 CXX_STANDARD 17)

# -ffast-math for the same reason as Flurry: particle simulation judged entirely by eye.
target_compile_options(savers PRIVATE -O2 -ffast-math -Wall -Wno-unused-parameter)
target_link_libraries(savers log GLESv2 m)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Discord Social SDK bridge -> libxeno_discord.so
#
# Separate target, and the manifest runs it in its own process. That is a
# LICENSING boundary, not a performance one: the Social SDK is proprietary with
# no published licence and the emulator core is GPL, so they must not share an
# address space.
#
# The prebuilt libdiscord_partner_sdk.so ships in the .aar too; it is referenced
# here as an IMPORTED target so the bridge links, and the .aar is what actually
# packages it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
if (CMAKE_SYSTEM_PROCESSOR MATCHES "aarch64")
    set(DISCORD_SDK_ROOT ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/discord_sdk)
    if (EXISTS ${DISCORD_SDK_ROOT}/arm64-v8a/libdiscord_partner_sdk.so)
        add_library(discord_partner_sdk SHARED IMPORTED)
        set_target_properties(discord_partner_sdk PROPERTIES
            IMPORTED_LOCATION ${DISCORD_SDK_ROOT}/arm64-v8a/libdiscord_partner_sdk.so)

        add_library(xeno_discord SHARED discord_bridge.cpp)
        target_include_directories(xeno_discord PRIVATE ${DISCORD_SDK_ROOT}/include)
        target_compile_features(xeno_discord PRIVATE cxx_std_17)
        target_link_libraries(xeno_discord discord_partner_sdk log android)
    else()
        message(STATUS "discord_sdk not staged (proprietary, not in git); building without the Discord helper")
    endif()
endif()

12:  *
13:  * The format is a fixed header, a table of fixed-size entries, then a key blob and a data blob:
14:  *
15:  *   header   magic "\0PSF", version, keyTableStart, dataTableStart, entryCount   (all LE)
16:  *   entry    keyOffset:u16 fmt:u16 len:u32 maxLen:u32 dataOffset:u32             (16 bytes)
17:  *   key      NUL-terminated string at keyTableStart + keyOffset
18:  *   data     at dataTableStart + dataOffset, `len` bytes, NUL-terminated when fmt is a string
19:  *
20:  * Only UTF-8 string values (fmt 0x0204) are returned; the fields worth showing are all strings
21:  * and an integer reader would be dead code.
22:  */
23: object Ps3Sfo {
24: 
25:     private const val MAGIC = 0x46535000 // "\0PSF" little-endian
26: 
27:     /** Parsed key/value pairs, or an empty map for anything that is not a readable SFO. */
28:     fun read(file: File): Map<String, String> = runCatching {
29:         if (!file.isFile || file.length() < 20 || file.length() > 1 shl 20) return emptyMap()
30: 
31:         val bytes = file.readBytes()
32: 
33:         fun u32(at: Int): Int =
34:             (bytes[at].toInt() and 0xff) or
35:                 ((bytes[at + 1].toInt() and 0xff) shl 8) or
36:                 ((bytes[at + 2].toInt() and 0xff) shl 16) or
37:                 ((bytes[at + 3].toInt() and 0xff) shl 24)
38: 
39:         fun u16(at: Int): Int = (bytes[at].toInt() and 0xff) or ((bytes[at + 1].toInt() and 0xff) shl 8)
40: 
41:         if (u32(0) != MAGIC) return emptyMap()
42: 
43:         val keyTable = u32(8)
44:         val dataTable = u32(12)
45:         val count = u32(16)
46: 
47:         // A corrupt or truncated file must read as "unknown", never throw into the UI.
48:         if (keyTable !in 0..bytes.size || dataTable !in 0..bytes.size || count !in 0..4096) {
49:             return emptyMap()
50:         }
51: 
52:         buildMap {
53:             for (i in 0 until count) {
54:                 val entry = 20 + i * 16
55:                 if (entry + 16 > bytes.size) break
56: 
57:                 val keyAt = keyTable + u16(entry)
58:                 val fmt = u16(entry + 2)
59:                 val len = u32(entry + 4)
60:                 val dataAt = dataTable + u32(entry + 12)
61: 
62:                 if (fmt != 0x0204) continue
63:                 if (keyAt !in 0 until bytes.size || len < 0) continue
64:                 if (dataAt < 0 || dataAt + len > bytes.size) continue
65: 
66:                 var keyEnd = keyAt
67:                 while (keyEnd < bytes.size && bytes[keyEnd].toInt() != 0) keyEnd++
68: 
69:                 val key = String(bytes, keyAt, keyEnd - keyAt, Charsets.UTF_8)
70: 
71:                 // Strings carry their terminator inside `len`.
72:                 var valueEnd = dataAt + len
73:                 while (valueEnd > dataAt && bytes[valueEnd - 1].toInt() == 0) valueEnd--
74: 
75:                 if (key.isNotEmpty()) {
76:                     put(key, String(bytes, dataAt, valueEnd - dataAt, Charsets.UTF_8))
77:                 }
78:             }
79:         }
80:     }.getOrDefault(emptyMap())

6:  * Serial + CRC for a disc image, resolved WITHOUT booting it.

8:  * The CRC used to appear only once a game had been launched, because every consumer read

10:  * the Info tab blank outside a game and made patch installs refuse outright, since the core only
11:  * loads `<SERIAL>_<CRC>.pnach` — you had to boot a game just to be allowed to install a patch for it.
12:  *
13:  * The capability already existed: `NativeApp.getGameTitle(path)` calls `GameList::PopulateEntryFromPath`,
14:  * which opens the image and computes serial and CRC with no VM at all. It had zero callers. This is
15:  * the wrapper it needed.
16:  *
17:  * **Blocking — never call from the main thread.** It reads the image's boot ELF (roughly 1–10 MB,
18:  * more for a compressed .chd, which decompresses on the way). Results are memoised per path for the
19:  * process lifetime; a disc image's identity cannot change without the file changing.
20:  */
21: object DiscIdentity {
22:     data class Id(val serial: String?, val crc: String?)
23: 
24:     private val cache = HashMap<String, Id>()
25: 
26:     /** Cached lookup, or null if the image could not be identified. */
27:     fun of(path: String): Id? {
28:         if (path.isBlank()) return null
29:         synchronized(cache) { cache[path]?.let { return it } }
30:         val id = probe(path) ?: return null
31:         synchronized(cache) { cache[path] = id }
32:         return id
33:     }
34: 
35:     /** Just the CRC as 8 uppercase hex digits, or null. */
36:     fun crcOf(path: String): String? = of(path)?.crc
37: 
38:     /** Same, from a [GameInfo]'s uri. Derives the native path exactly as the launcher does
39:      *  (MainActivityRuntime's launchPath), so identity and boot always agree on the same file. */
40:     fun of(uri: android.net.Uri): Id? = of(nativePath(uri))
41: 
42:     fun crcOf(uri: android.net.Uri): String? = of(uri)?.crc
43: 
44:     /** Eight hex digits, as CRCs are rendered and as PNACH filenames spell them. */
45:     val CRC_PATTERN = Regex("[0-9A-Fa-f]{8}")
46: 
47:     /**
48:      * The CRC for [game], preferring the running VM and falling back to identifying the image.
49:      *
50:      * One copy, called from the Info tab and from the library's long-press sheet. It was already
51:      * duplicated once; a third copy was going to drift.
52:      *
53:      * Reads the VM only when the serial it reports matches this game — otherwise a different
54:      * running game would lend its CRC to whatever the user long-pressed.
55:      */

57:         kotlinx.coroutines.withContext(kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers.IO) {
58:             runCatching {
59:                 val wanted = serial?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() }
60:                 if (wanted != null &&

65:                         ?.uppercase()

## 2. IS a game vs IS NOT a game — exact rules and constants

### 2a. File extension whitelist (the only extension filter)

`GameLibraryRepository.kt:30–32`:
```kotlin
private val gameExtensions = setOf(
    "iso", "chd", "cso", "zso", "gz", "bin", "mdf", "img", "nrg", "dump", "elf",
)
```
**There is NO `.pkg`, `.ps3`, `.ps1`, `.ps2`, or `.m3u` in the scanner's whitelist.** Those only appear:


### 2b. Recursion and depth

### 2c. FOLDERS ARE treated as games — `isPs3GameFolder`

`GameLibraryRepository.kt:422–444` (full body):
```kotlin
private fun isPs3GameFolder(directory: File): Boolean {
    fun child(vararg path: String): File? {
        var current: File = directory
        for (segment in path) {
            current = current.listFiles()
                ?.firstOrNull { it.name.equals(segment, ignoreCase = true) }
                ?: return null
        }
        return current
    }
    if (child("PS3_GAME", "PARAM.SFO")?.isFile == true) return true
    if (child("PS3_DISC.SFB")?.isFile == true) return true
    val sfo = child("PARAM.SFO")?.takeIf { it.isFile } ?: return false
    if (child("USRDIR")?.isDirectory != true) return false
    // ... data-install rejection ...
    return sfoCategory(sfo) != "GD"
}
```

**Exact constants recognised as "this folder IS a game":**

| Pattern | Meaning | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `PS3_GAME/PARAM.SFO` | JB folder dump (case-insensitive) | 432 |
| `PS3_DISC.SFB` | real disc rip (case-insensitive), alone is enough | 433 |
| `PARAM.SFO` + `USRDIR/` (dir) | installed/HDD game folder | 434–435 |
| `PARAM.SFO` CATEGORY `!= "GD"` | excludes game-data installs | 443 |

Notably **`game.iso` inside a folder is NOT how folders are recognised** — there is no such check. A folder containing only `game.iso` is *not* a game folder; the `.iso` is found by the normal file branch and listed individually.

Case-insensitivity is explicit (comment 418–420: FAT/exFAT → `PS3_GAME` as likely to be `ps3_game`).

**A game folder is a LEAF** — `scanRawDirectory:505–519`:
```kotlin
if (file.isDirectory) {
    // A game folder is a leaf: emit it and do NOT descend. ...
    if (runCatching { isPs3GameFolder(file) }.getOrDefault(false)) {
        val folderUri = Uri.fromFile(file)
        output.putIfAbsent(folderUri.toString(),
            createGame(folderUri, file.name, "folder", null, probeDisc(file)))
        return@forEach
    }
    scanRawDirectory(file, output, depth + 1)
    return@forEach
}
```
The pseudo-extension used for folders is the **literal string `"folder"`** (uppercased to `"FOLDER"` in `GameInfo.extension` by `createGame` line 640). Read back at line 220: `game.extension.equals("folder", ignoreCase = true)`.
